Singapore East (Katong/Joo Chiat, Geylang, Bedok, Tampines, Changi)

cuisines.n: Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee)

P.ad: 135 Nam Ky Khoi Nghia, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: The modernist 1960s presidential palace where NVA Tank 843 crashed the gate on 30 April 1975, ending the war. Frozen-in-time state rooms, war-command bunker and telecoms basement. National monument; daily ~07:00-18:00, 80,000d.

P.ad: 01 Cong xa Paris, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: The twin-spired red-brick French cathedral (1863-1880) built with imported Marseille materials, on the square opposite the Post Office. UNDER RESTORATION since 2017 (interior closed to visitors; completion pushed to ~2027, scaffolding coming off by early 2026) — view the exterior.

P.ad: 125 Cong xa Paris (Hai Ba Trung), Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: Working 1886-1891 post office (architect Alfred Foulhoux; often mis-credited to Eiffel) with a vaulted iron-truss hall, painted maps and a portrait of Ho Chi Minh. Ranked among the world's most beautiful post offices; still operational.

P.ad: 73 Mai Thi Luu, Da Kao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: Saigon's most atmospheric Taoist temple, built by the Cantonese community in 1909, thick with incense smoke and carved wooden deities incl. the Hall of Ten Hells and a turtle pond. Obama visited in 2016. Free, ~07:00-18:00.

P.n: Nguyen Hue Walking Street & People's Committee Building
P.ad: Nguyen Hue Boulevard, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: The city's 900 m pedestrian boulevard (a former canal, walkerised 2015) running from the floodlit French Hotel de Ville / People's Committee Building (1898-1909, viewed from outside) and Ho Chi Minh statue down to the Saigon River. Liveliest at night.

P.ad: 07 Cong Truong Lam Son, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: Flamboyant 1897-1900 French Beaux-Arts theatre, once seat of South Vietnam's Lower House, now a national relic staging the acclaimed bamboo-circus A O Show and The Mist.

P.ad: 36 Ho Tung Mau, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: The 262 m lotus-bud tower (2010) with a helipad wing and the 49th-floor Saigon Skydeck, the city's first observation deck, giving 360-degree views over the river. Open daily ~09:30-21:30.

P.n: Ho Chi Minh City Museum (Gia Long Palace)
P.ad: 65 Ly Tu Trong, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: City-history museum in an 1885-1890 neoclassical palace that served the French governor, President Diem (as Gia Long Palace) and the RVN Supreme Court, with a wartime bunker/tunnel beneath. Traces Saigon from prehistory to reunification.

P.ad: 2 Nguyen Binh Khiem, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: Vietnam's national-history collection in a 1926-1929 Indochinese-style building beside the Botanical Gardens: Cham and Oc Eo antiquities, Dong Son drums, a mummified noblewoman, plus water-puppet shows. Closed Mondays.

P.n: Fine Arts Museum (Bao tang My thuat)
P.ad: 97A Pho Duc Chinh, Nguyen Thai Binh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: The city's leading art museum in a yellow 1929-1934 Franco-Chinese mansion of the wealthy Hua family, with the first lift in Saigon; holds lacquer, silk and war-era painting plus Champa/Oc Eo relics. Closed Mondays.

P.ad: 42 Nguyen Hue, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A crumbling 1960s nine-storey block (once housing for US advisers) reborn as a vertical warren of independent cafes, boutiques and bars, each balcony overlooking the walking street. Slow lift ~3,000d, or take the stairs.

P.n: Book Street (Duong Sach Nguyen Van Binh)
P.ad: Nguyen Van Binh, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A shaded 144 m pedestrian lane beside the cathedral and Post Office lined with 20-plus publisher stalls, secondhand-book stands and book cafes, plus author events. Free; best in the evening.

P.ad: Bui Vien Street, Pham Ngu Lao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: Saigon's neon backpacker strip in the Pham Ngu Lao quarter (on the map since Lonely Planet's 1993 guide) — bar stools spilling into the road, street food and live music. Pedestrianised nightly; peaks Fri-Sun.

P.n: Ho Chi Minh Museum - Dragon House Wharf (Nha Rong)
P.ad: 1 Nguyen Tat Thanh, District 4, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: The 1862-1863 twin-dragon-roofed former Messageries Maritimes house on the riverfront from which the 21-year-old future Ho Chi Minh sailed to France in June 1911; a branch of the Ho Chi Minh Museum since 1979. Closed Mondays.

P.ad: Cong Truong Quoc Te (Pham Ngoc Thach / Tran Cao Van), District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A modernist 1967-1972 traffic-circle monument of five splayed concrete 'hands' and an octagonal fountain, on the site of a French water tower and an old Nguyen-era citadel gate. Now a beloved evening hangout for street snacks.

P.ad: 202 Vo Thi Sau, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A 31,000-object museum (est. 1985; Class-I museum from 2024) devoted to southern Vietnamese women in war and culture — female guerrillas, ao dai history and Mother Goddess worship. Closed Mondays; free.

P.ad: 5 Ton Duc Thang, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: Riverside museum (opened 1988) to Ton Duc Thang, Vietnam's second president and a Con Dao political prisoner, with 16,000+ documents on his life and the labour movement. Closed Mondays; free.

P.ad: 104 Yersin, Nguyen Thai Binh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: The 'American Market' off Yersin St, famous since 1975 for army-surplus gear, dog tags, ponchos and militaria (genuine and replica) alongside hardware stalls — a gritty relic of the war years. Bargain and check provenance.

P.ad: 339 Nam Ky Khoi Nghia, Ward 7, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: The city's largest Mahayana pagoda (built 1964-1971 with Japanese aid), the first to render traditional temple form in concrete, crowned by a seven-storey, 40 m stupa. Free.

P.ad: 89 Ba Huyen Thanh Quan, Vo Thi Sau Ward, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A seven-storey 1956-1958 pagoda that was the flashpoint of the 1963 Buddhist Crisis: the epicentre of anti-Diem protests and the 21 August 1963 army raid that arrested hundreds of monks and helped trigger the coup.

P.ad: 289 Hai Ba Trung, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: The bubblegum-pink Romano-Gothic Catholic church begun 1870-1876 (its signature pink dates to a 1957 repaint) — the city's second-largest church and a landmark photo stop. Active parish; exterior always, interior around Mass times.

P.ad: 720A Dien Bien Phu, Ward 22, Binh Thanh District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: At 461 m the tallest building in Vietnam (2018), a bamboo-cluster supertall over the Saigon River in Vinhomes Central Park. The SkyView observatory spans floors 79-81 for the city's highest panorama.

P.ad: 710 Nguyen Trai, Ward 11, District 5 (Cholon), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: Cholon's most famous temple (Tue Thanh Guildhall), built by Cantonese immigrants around 1760 for Mazu, sea goddess of the overseas Chinese. Famed for its porcelain-figurine roof friezes and hanging incense coils. National monument.

P.ad: 57A Thap Muoi, Ward 2, District 6 (Cholon), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: Cholon's grand wholesale market, financed by merchant Quach Dam and completed 1928, built around a pagoda-roofed courtyard; a recognised heritage building (restored 2016-2018) and still a major distribution hub.

P.ad: 25 Hoc Lac, Ward 14, District 5 (Cholon), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: Cholon's Chinese-Catholic parish church (1900-1902), Gothic with Chinese detailing. Here President Ngo Dinh Diem and his brother took refuge and surrendered during the 1 November 1963 coup, before being killed en route.

P.ad: 678 Nguyen Trai, Ward 11, District 5 (Cholon), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A 19th-century Teochew guildhall temple to the deified warlord Quan Cong, one of Cholon's oldest, celebrated for its gilded woodwork, a huge red-lacquer horse of Quan Cong and intricate roof ceramics.

P.ad: 264 Hai Thuong Lan Ong, Ward 14, District 5 (Cholon), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A Fujianese assembly-hall temple (Nhi Phu Hoi Quan, from the late 17th/18th c.) venerating Ong Bon, guardian god of land and wealth; ship-prow roofs, carved red pillars and a national relic listing (1998).

P.ad: 802 Nguyen Trai, Ward 14, District 5 (Cholon), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A southern-Fujian (Zhangzhou) guildhall temple founded 1809 for Thien Hau, with four China-carved dragon-wrapped stone pillars shipped in by boat and vivid ceramic roof scenes; especially alive at the Lantern Festival.

P.ad: 565 Lac Long Quan, Ward 10, Tan Binh District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: Believed the oldest temple in the city (founded 1744), atmospheric in garden grounds with a Bodhi tree, a nine-tier stupa and thousands of decorative plates set into its walls. National relic. Free.

P.ad: Long Hoa, Hoa Thanh, Tay Ninh Province, Vietnam (day trip ~90 km NW of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam)
P.w: The kaleidoscopic 1933-1955 Great Temple of Caodaism, Vietnam's homegrown syncretic religion, with a divine 'all-seeing eye', dragon pillars and rainbow interior. Time a visit for the white-robed noon ceremony. Often paired with Cu Chi.

P.n: Mekong Delta Day Trip (My Tho & Ben Tre)
P.ad: My Tho (Tien Giang) & Ben Tre Provinces, Vietnam (day trip ~70-90 km SW of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam)
P.w: The classic close Delta day trip: a Tien River cruise past the Dragon/Unicorn/Phoenix/Tortoise islets, sampan rides through coconut-palm canals, a coconut-candy workshop, honey tea and the large Vinh Trang Pagoda at My Tho.

P.ad: Ninh Son, Tay Ninh Province, Vietnam (day trip ~100 km NW of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam)
P.w: The 986 m 'Black Virgin Mountain', highest peak in the south, a pilgrimage site of cave temples reached by a Guinness-record cable-car system to Sun World, with a 72 m bronze Bodhisattva at the summit. Pairs with Tay Ninh's Cao Dai temple.

P.n: Can Gio Mangrove Biosphere Reserve (Monkey Island)
P.ad: Can Gio District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam (~50-60 km SE of the centre)
P.w: Vietnam's first UNESCO Man-and-Biosphere reserve (designated 2000), a replanted mangrove forest that was the Viet Cong's Rung Sac guerrilla zone. Boat trips, a reconstructed guerrilla base, crocodile lagoons and a large troop of macaques ('Monkey Island').

P.ad: Cai Rang District, Can Tho, Mekong Delta, Vietnam (long day trip / overnight ~170 km SW of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam)
P.w: The biggest floating wholesale market in the Delta, where boats trade produce hung from tall poles at dawn on the Can Tho River. Deep in the Delta (~3.5 hrs each way) — best as an early-start long day trip or overnight; trades wind down by ~08:30.

P.ad: Ha Long St, Ward 2, Vung Tau, Ba Ria-Vung Tau Province, Vietnam (day trip ~95 km / 2-hr ferry from Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam)
P.w: The nearest beach escape: a seaside town crowned by a 32 m Christ the King statue (1974) you can climb (~800 steps inside) for coastal views, plus the White Palace and Back Beach. Reachable by road or Saigon River fast ferry.

P.ad: 45 Truong Dinh, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: Saigon's only Hindu temple, a vivid South-Indian shrine built by Tamil merchants in the late 1800s to the goddess Mariamman, its ~12 m gopuram crowded with painted deities. Free; daily ~07:00-19:00, remove shoes.

P.n: Ho Thi Ky Flower & Food Market
P.ad: Ho Thi Ky Street (Alley 52), Ward 1, District 10, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A 24-hour wholesale flower market (blooms trucked in nightly from Da Lat) wrapped in a warren of alleys that turn into one of Saigon's best night food streets, heavy with Khmer-Vietnamese 'Little Cambodia' dishes. Liveliest in the evening.

P.ad: Truong Dinh Street, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: One of central Saigon's largest green spaces (a former French garden), with a Cham-style shrine, a Hung Kings temple and a famous early-morning 'bird cafe' where locals hang songbird cages (~06:00-09:00; disrupted in recent years by Metro works). Free.

P.ad: 1 Ton That Tung (corner Nguyen Trai), Nguyen Cu Trinh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A serene 1902-05 Gothic Catholic church funded by Le Phat Dat (Huyen Sy), once the richest man in the south and great-grandfather of Vietnam's last queen, with a granite-and-stained-glass nave and the founders' tombs behind the chancel. Free.

P.ad: 81 Nguyen Xien, Long Binh Ward, Thu Duc City, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A gleaming white Thai/Indian-style Theravada temple and 56 m Gotama Cetiya stupa on a hill above the Dong Nai River in Thu Duc, named by National Geographic (2019) among the world's 10 most beautiful Buddhist sites. Free; incense-free grounds.

P.ad: 1147 Binh Quoi, Ward 28 (Thanh Da Peninsula), Binh Thanh District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A riverside 'traditional-village' recreation park on the Thanh Da peninsula run by Saigontourist, known for its weekend Southern-style buffets, folk games and thatched-hut gardens along the Saigon River. Free entry; paid activities and buffet.

P.ad: 66 Dong Du, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A calm blue-and-white 1935 mosque built by South-Indian Muslim traders on a busy District 1 street, the largest in the city and a quiet oasis behind the Dong Du shops. Open daily; dress modestly, busiest at Friday midday.

P.ad: 336 Hai Ba Trung (corner Nguyen Huu Cau), Tan Dinh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A striking 1926-27 French market hall with a butter-yellow facade and three towers, now the city's best-known fabric market (ao dai silks) ringed by a wet-market and street-food stalls. Daily ~05:00-18:00.

P.n: Le Van Duyet Tomb (Lang Ong Ba Chieu)
P.ad: 1 Vu Tung, Ward 1 (Ba Chieu), Binh Thanh District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: The walled tomb-temple of Marshal Le Van Duyet (1763-1832), the eunuch viceroy of Gia Dinh, one of the city's oldest and most revered shrines and a recognised national relic; thronged during the Ky Yen festival. Free, beside Ba Chieu Market.

P.n: Saigon Zoo & Botanical Gardens (Thao Cam Vien)
P.ad: 2 Nguyen Binh Khiem, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: Founded 1864-65, one of the world's eight oldest continuously operating zoos: a 20 ha park of century-old trees, colonial-era buildings and the Hung Kings temple alongside the animal enclosures. Daily; ticketed.

P.n: Quan Am Pagoda (On Lang Assembly Hall)
P.ad: 12 Lao Tu, Ward 11, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A 1740 Fujianese temple in Cholon dedicated to Guanyin, one of the district's oldest and most ornate, with elaborate ceramic roof friezes, shard-mosaic reliefs and gilded carvings. Free, ~06:00-18:00.

P.ad: Thu Thiem Ward, Thu Duc City (District 2), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A 20 ha riverfront park opened December 2023 on the Thu Thiem side, with a ~3.7 km promenade, lawns and cycling paths facing the District 1 skyline; the classic spot for sunset and floodlit night skyline views. Open 24h, free.

P.ad: 41 Hoang Du Khuong, Ward 12, District 10, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A private museum (opened 2007) in a reconstructed traditional wooden house of ~18 rooms, with 3,000+ artifacts of Vietnamese herbal medicine, an old apothecary shop and pressing and decoction tools. Daily ~08:30-17:00; ticketed.

P.ad: 244 Ba Tháng Hai, Ward 12, District 10, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A landmark District 10 Buddhist temple on Ba Tháng Hai (3/2) Boulevard, originally built in 1964 and rebuilt 2014–2017 around a soaring 13-storey stupa (Tháp Đa Bảo). A historically significant seat of Vietnamese Buddhism and a striking, uncrowded stop; upper floors open on the 1st and 15th of the lunar month.

P.ad: Vĩnh Khánh Street (Bến Vân Đồn to Tôn Đản), Ward 8 & Ward 9, District 4, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: District 4's famous after-dark ốc (snail) and seafood strip — nearly a kilometre of charcoal grills and plastic-stool eateries that fire up around dusk and run past midnight. Officially designated a Saigon food street in 2018 and named by VnExpress among the world's coolest snail streets; the single most concentrated street-seafood experience in the city (Ốc Oanh, a MICHELIN Selected snail house, anchors it).

P.ad: 24 Chánh Hưng, Ward 4, District 8, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A near-180-year-old Buddhist temple in District 8 whose surfaces are almost entirely mosaicked in over 30 tonnes of broken porcelain and ceramic shards — bowls, plates, teapots — applied by hand from 1961 to 2004. Holds a Vietnam Book of Records mark for the most ceramic pieces, plus a pair of 3.4 m, 1.8-tonne candles. The 'Miểng Sành' pagoda is District 8's signature sight.

P.ad: Cù lao Bà Tàng, Ward 7, District 8, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A communal house of more than 150 years standing alone on a two-hectare islet in the Kênh Đôi canal, granted a royal decree by Emperor Tự Đức in 1853 and ranked a national historic-cultural relic. Reached by a short ferry hop, it is a highlight of District 8's on-the-water heritage tours — a rare Nam Bộ đình marooned mid-canal.

P.n: Bến Bình Đông & the Tết Flower Market
P.ad: Bến Bình Đông (along Kênh Tàu Hủ), Ward 11, District 8, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: The old rice-trade wharf strung along Kênh Tàu Hủ, once the 'prosperous Tàu Hủ avenue' linking Saigon-Chợ Lớn to the Mekong. Each Lunar New Year it becomes the 'trên bến dưới thuyền' flower market, with growers selling blooms straight off sampans — the most atmospheric Tết scene in the city and a working glimpse of canal-borne Saigon.

P.ad: Nguyễn Văn Linh, Ward 7, District 8, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: The largest wholesale market in Vietnam, a 65-hectare complex in far-southwest District 8 and the biggest seafood distribution hub in the south. It runs through the night — hundreds of tonnes of fish, produce and flowers moving from about 1am to 11am. Not a polished tourist stop but an extraordinary look at how the city is fed.

P.ad: Đỗ Năng Tế, Bình Trị Đông A Ward, Bình Tân, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: One of Saigon's oldest temples and the flagship Buddhist sight of Bình Tân, famed for extraordinary woodwork: ironwood doors carved with the 12 zodiac animals and eight vajra guardians (a Vietnam record), and giant fragrant-wood Buddhas including a 16-tonne, 8 m Amitabha billed as the tallest wooden Buddha statue in the country.

P.ad: Cầu Nhị Thiên Đường (over Kênh Đôi), Ward 5, District 8, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A 1925 bridge over the Kênh Đôi, said to be the first reinforced-concrete bridge in Indochina, built by the Chinese-Vietnamese magnate behind the Nhị Thiên Đường medicated-oil empire. A row of arches beneath it evokes an old Roman viaduct; a District 8 landmark and marker of the Nam Bộ resistance era.

P.ad: 1 Đường số 17A, Bình Trị Đông B Ward, Bình Tân, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: The 114,000 sqm Japanese-run mall that anchors Bình Tân, opened 2016 as one of the largest in Ho Chi Minh City — cinema, a huge food street, and the everyday air-conditioned pull for the district's working-class west. The practical family day-out landmark out here.

P.ad: Chợ Xóm Củi, Ward 10, District 8, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A decades-old District 8 market whose name ('firewood hamlet') recalls the canal-side firewood depots that once supplied Chợ Lớn. It grew from those wood yards into the district's central market of hundreds of stalls — a dense, cheap street-food warren and a window on working-class Rạch Ông life.

P.ad: Islet in the Vàm Thuật River, ferry from end of Trần Bá Giao St, Ward 5, Gò Vấp, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A ~300-year-old 'floating temple' on a 2,500 m² islet in the middle of the Vàm Thuật River, reached only by a short ferry (~10k VND). More than 100 colourful ceramic-mosaic dragons cover the roofs and columns of the Buddhist-Taoist shrine, a city-recognised architectural-artistic heritage site since 2010. One of Gò Vấp's few genuine landmarks.

P.ad: 1460 Phan Văn Hớn, Xuân Thới Thượng Commune, Hóc Môn, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A 73,000 m² national historical monument (ranked 2002) on the site where French colonial authorities executed revolutionary leaders after the failed 1940 Nam Kỳ (Southern) Uprising. A memorial temple, exhibition house and monuments sit among bamboo, lotus ponds and areca palms — the anchor heritage site of rural Hóc Môn.

P.n: Bà Điểm & the Eighteen Betel Garden Villages (18 Thôn Vườn Trầu)
P.ad: Bà Điểm Commune, Hóc Môn, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: The historic areca-and-betel-growing belt around Bà Điểm, famed since the 18th century and a cradle of the 1940 Southern Uprising — the Southern Party Committee sheltered in its gardens. Today a living cultural-heritage landscape of remnant trầu (betel) gardens and revolutionary memory rather than a ticketed attraction.

P.ad: 30 Bờ Bao Tân Thắng, Sơn Kỳ Ward, Tân Phú, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: AEON's first shopping mall in Vietnam, opened 11 Jan 2014 — a ~70,000 m² Japanese-anchored complex in the Celadon City estate that made Vietnam the third country (after Malaysia and China) with a large-scale AEON MALL. A CGV cinema, food court, indoor playground and 200+ brands make it the western suburbs' main weekend gathering place.

P.ad: 120 Hanoi Highway, Tan Phu Ward, Thu Duc City, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: The world's first Buddhism-themed amusement/water park (opened 1995), a surreal 200-ha spread of giant dragons, a neon-haloed Buddha shrine, a 'Buddhist Hell' walkthrough and waterslides pouring from sages' beards. ~1.5-2M visitors/year; daily ~07:30-17:00. Reachable on Metro Line 1.

P.n: Vietnam National Historical Culture Park (Cong vien Lich su Van hoa Dan toc)
P.ad: Long Binh Ward, Thu Duc (District 9), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A ~400-ha state park recreating Vietnam's history in themed zones, anchored by the grand Hung Kings temple complex where the city holds its official Hung Kings' Death Anniversary rites. Long-running build-out; the ancient/Hung-Kings zone is the finished, visit-worthy core.

P.n: Crescent Mall & Starlight Bridge (Cau Anh Sao)
P.ad: Ton Dat Tien, Phu My Hung, District 7, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: The centrepiece of planned Phu My Hung: a 170 m LED-lit pedestrian bridge over crescent-shaped Ho Ban Nguyet lake, glowing like a starry sky at night, beside the riverfront Crescent Mall. The go-to evening promenade of Saigon's affluent south.

P.ad: Hoang Van Thu, Tan Binh District (by Tan Son Nhat Airport), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A triangular 10.6-ha green lung immediately south of Tan Son Nhat airport, ringed by three boulevards, with lakes, shaded paths and a children's playground; open 24/7, free. The most convenient park for a stopover near the airport.

P.ad: Huynh Van Nghe, Buu Long Ward, Bien Hoa, Dong Nai, Vietnam
P.w: An 84-ha scenic park nicknamed the 'Ha Long Bay of the South' for the limestone crags rising from emerald Long An lake (a flooded quarry), with boating, gardens and hilltop pagodas. ~30 km from central HCMC; open ~07:00-17:00 (closed Tuesdays).

P.n: Cu Lao Pho & That Phu Ancient Temple (Ong Pagoda)
P.ad: Hiep Hoa (Cu Lao Pho), Bien Hoa, Dong Nai, Vietnam
P.w: A Dong Nai river island that was the South's busiest trading port in the 1700s, founded by Chinese refugee Tran Thuong Xuyen; today a cluster of national-relic shrines, led by That Phu Ancient Temple (c.1684, the earliest Chinese temple in southern Vietnam) and Dai Giac Pagoda.

P.ad: Vinh Cuu District, Tri An, Dong Nai, Vietnam
P.w: Vietnam's largest man-made reservoir (behind the Tri An hydro dam), a vast expanse dotted with ~76 forested islets, popular for boat trips, sunrise/sunset floats, island picnics and overnight fishing with local boatmen. ~65-70 km northeast of HCMC.

P.n: Dai Nam Wonderland (Dai Nam Van Hien)
P.ad: Dai Nam, Thu Dau Mot, Binh Duong, Vietnam
P.w: Vietnam's largest tourist complex (711 ha, opened 2008): an amusement park, a man-made 'sea' with wave beach, a zoo/safari, a racecourse and the colossal gilded Kim Dien (Dai Nam) temple, once the country's biggest. ~40 km north of HCMC.

P.ad: 4 Nguyen Du, Phu Cuong Ward, Thu Dau Mot, Binh Duong, Vietnam
P.w: The Hoa (Chinese-Vietnamese) community's Mazu temple in Thu Dau Mot and the heart of the Chua Ba Festival on the 15th of the first lunar month, when a palanquin procession with 30+ lion-dance troupes draws hundreds of thousands through the town.

P.ad: Lai Thieu, Thuan An, Binh Duong, Vietnam
P.w: A ~1,200-ha belt of riverside garden orchards famed for mangosteen and durian, where farms run agritourism visits, canal boat rides and fruit buffets in hammock-slung gardens. Season peaks May-August; the classic Saigon weekend fruit-picking escape.

P.n: Ben Duoc Memorial Temple (Den Ben Duoc)
P.ad: Phu My Hung Commune, Cu Chi, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A solemn state memorial temple at the far end of the Cu Chi tunnel zone, inscribed with the names of ~45,000 martyrs of the Saigon-Gia Dinh region; a 7-ha compound of carved murals and a nine-storey tower. The reflective counterpart to the tunnels' war-tourism.

P.ad: Ly Nhon Commune, Can Gio, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A ticketed eco-centre deep in the UNESCO Can Gio mangrove biosphere and a designated Ramsar site: a stork/heron bird sanctuary, a bat lagoon, a crocodile swamp and a watchtower over the wetlands. Distinct from the Monkey Island site, and the birders' pick.

P.ad: 1A Tran Phu (Nui Lon), Vung Tau, Vietnam
P.w: A 100-ha mountaintop leisure park on Nui Lon reached by cable car, with a summit lake, gardens, a nightly musical-fountain 'Grand Show' and sweeping panoramas over Vung Tau and the sea.

P.ad: Hai Dang, Ward 2 (Nui Nho), Vung Tau, Vietnam
P.w: Built by the French in 1862, the oldest of Vietnam's ~79 lighthouses, perched atop Nui Nho (Small Mountain); a short climb up 55 steps delivers a 360-degree view over the city, harbour and the Christ statue on the opposite hill.

P.ad: Thuy Van, Bai Sau, Vung Tau, Vietnam
P.w: Vung Tau's main swimming beach, a ~10 km southeast-facing strand lined with loungers, seafood shacks and water sports (surf, SUP, kite-surf); the Saigonese weekend seaside default, two hours from the city.

P.ad: Hai Ba Trung, Ninh Kieu, Can Tho, Vietnam
P.w: The riverfront symbol of Can Tho: a promenade park on the Hau River (named 1958) with a Ho Chi Minh statue, the Can Tho cable-stayed bridge views, the arched Ninh Kieu pedestrian bridge and an adjacent night market; the launch point for Cai Rang floating-market boats.

P.ad: Nguyen Trung Truc, My Phong, My Tho, Tien Giang, Vietnam
P.w: The largest and most famous pagoda in Tien Giang (completed 1850), a national heritage site blending Vietnamese, Khmer, Chinese and European arches, set in gardens with giant Buddha statues; the standout stop on any My Tho / Mekong day trip.

P.n: Sun World Ba Đen Mountain Cable Car
P.ad: Sun World Ba Den Mountain, Núi Bà Đen, Tây Ninh, Vietnam
P.w: The Doppelmayr cable-car complex that lifts you up the 986 m 'Roof of the South' in minutes instead of a three-hour climb. Its Ba Den departure station holds the Guinness World Record for the largest cable-car station (10,959 sqm), moving 4,400 passengers an hour to the spiritual complex on top.

P.n: Tây Bổ Đà Sơn Buddha Statue
P.ad: Summit of Núi Bà Đen, Tây Ninh, Vietnam
P.w: A 72 m bronze Bodhisattva cast from 170+ tonnes of red copper on the 986 m summit — recognised by Guinness as Asia's tallest bronze Lady-Buddha statue on a mountain peak. Ringed by terraced gardens and often wrapped in cloud, it is the visual icon of the Bà Đen complex.

P.n: Ma Thiên Lãnh Valley & Núi Đá Lake
P.ad: Thạnh Tân, Tây Ninh (Ma Thiên Lãnh), Vietnam
P.w: A cool green valley cradled between Bà Đen, Núi Heo and Núi Phụng, nicknamed 'the Đà Lạt of the Southeast'. Its emerald Núi Đá Lake — a flooded former limestone quarry ringed by primeval forest — is the region's favourite camping, BBQ and photo spot.

P.ad: Dầu Tiếng, Tây Ninh, Vietnam
P.w: Vietnam and Southeast Asia's largest artificial lake — 270 sqkm damming the upper Saigon River, completed 1985 — now an ecotourism draw of forested islets and hill-fringed water. A go-to for camping, fishing and sunset-watching on the far side of Bà Đen.

P.ad: Long Hoa, Hòa Thành, Tây Ninh, Vietnam
P.w: Tây Ninh's busiest market, laid out in 1952 to the design of Cao Đài dignitary Phạm Công Tắc to serve the faith's followers. The place to buy the province's edible souvenirs — dew-soaked rice paper, muối tôm, sesame and beans — and to eat at its famous vegetarian stalls.

P.n: Cu Chi Wildlife Rescue Station — CLOSED
P.ad: Tỉnh lộ 15, between Bến Đình & Bến Dược, Củ Chi, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: An NGO-run rescue centre (founded 2006, Wildlife at Risk) between the two tunnel sites that rehabilitated 4,000+ trafficked animals — pangolins, bears, otters, gibbons, langurs — with a public education display. Now closed to visitors indefinitely; listed for reference.

P.ad: 78 Sông Lu, Trung An, Củ Chi, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A cluster of pick-your-own orchards 30 km out in Trung An commune — rambutan, mangosteen, jackfruit and durian in season — where a small entry fee lets you eat fruit off the tree and try Củ Chi country snacks. A relaxed rural add-on to the tunnels.

P.ad: 10 Trần Phú, Phường 1, Vũng Tàu, Bà Rịa–Vũng Tàu, Vietnam
P.w: A colonial villa built 1898–1902 for Governor-General Paul Doumer on the old Phước Thắng Fortress hill, later a retreat for Emperor Bảo Đại and a place of exile for Emperor Thành Thái. A national historical relic (1992) overlooking Front Beach, now housing an antiques collection.

P.ad: off Mũi Nghinh Phong / Bãi Sau, Phường 2, Vũng Tàu, Bà Rịa–Vũng Tàu, Vietnam
P.w: A tiny rocky islet crowned by a small temple locals hold sacred; at low tide a natural stone causeway surfaces so you can walk out from the shore. A quiet sunrise and spiritual spot — time it carefully or the rising tide strands you.

P.ad: Quang Trung / Trần Phú promenade, Bãi Trước, Vũng Tàu, Bà Rịa–Vũng Tàu, Vietnam
P.w: Vũng Tàu's crescent-bay waterfront between Big and Small Mountain — a palm-lined promenade for sunset strolls, seafood and coconuts, ringed by landmarks (Bạch Dinh, the cable-car station, Phước Thắng Fortress). The city's social heart, quieter than Back Beach.

P.ad: 608 Trần Phú, Núi Lớn, Phường 5, Vũng Tàu, Bà Rịa–Vũng Tàu, Vietnam
P.w: A five-hectare Theravada Buddhist complex on the northwest slope of Big Mountain, built 1961–1963: a 10m+ golden seated Buddha among pines and a 17m octagonal reliquary tower holding relics and sacred earth from Buddhist holy sites. Designated a national relic in 1989.

P.n: Nhà Lớn Long Sơn (Đền Ông Trần)
P.ad: Long Sơn commune (Núi Nứa island), Vũng Tàu, Bà Rịa–Vũng Tàu, Vietnam
P.w: A one-of-a-kind 2-hectare wood-and-tile temple compound on Long Sơn island, built 1910–1929 by Lê Văn Mưu ('Ông Trần'), founder of a local folk faith blending Confucianism and Taoism. Temple, mausoleum and communal halls with a century-old tamarind tree; a national relic and the island's living heritage site.

P.ad: Đường Dinh Cô, Long Hải, Long Điền, Bà Rịa–Vũng Tàu, Vietnam
P.w: A seaside shrine on Long Hải beach to a 19th-century maiden revered as a sea goddess, and site of the Dinh Cô Festival (10th–12th of the 2nd lunar month) — a Mother-Goddess worship rite recognised as National Intangible Cultural Heritage, with boat processions, lion dances and beach games.

P.n: Bình Châu Hot Springs (Suối khoáng nóng Bình Châu)
P.ad: Bình Châu, Xuyên Mộc, Bà Rịa–Vũng Tàu, Vietnam
P.w: Southern Vietnam's only natural hot mineral springs — 70-plus surface vents from 37°C up to a boiling 82°C, set in the Bình Châu–Phước Bửu coastal forest with soaking pools, mud baths and an egg-boiling spring. A classic overnight on the Hồ Tràm–Hồ Cốc coast road.

P.ad: Bưng Riềng, Xuyên Mộc, Bà Rịa–Vũng Tàu, Vietnam
P.w: One of the most pristine beaches near Saigon — several kilometres of white sand backed by the Bình Châu–Phước Bửu forest, with clear water, big boulders and cheap fresh seafood. Reached on the scenic Ocean Road from Hồ Tràm, about 20 minutes from Bình Châu hot springs.

P.ad: Hồ Tràm, Phước Thuận, Xuyên Mộc, Bà Rịa–Vũng Tàu, Vietnam
P.w: A long, quiet arc of fine sand and clear water between Long Hải and Bình Châu, ~125 km from HCMC — casuarina-lined, cheap seafood at the fishing hamlet, and the anchor of the coast's cluster of beach resorts and golf courses. With Hồ Cốc, the best beach within easy reach of Saigon.

P.ad: Bình Châu / Bưng Riềng, Xuyên Mộc, Bà Rịa–Vũng Tàu, Vietnam
P.w: An 11,293-hectare protected coastal rainforest — the region's only surviving lowland dipterocarp forest — wrapping the Hồ Tràm and Hồ Cốc beaches and the Bình Châu hot springs. Home to the 136m Núi Hồ Linh hill and endangered species; hiking trails through a rare intact ecosystem.

P.n: Khu Du Lịch Sinh Thái Bò Cạp Vàng
P.ad: Ấp 3, Phước Khánh, Nhơn Trạch, Đồng Nai, Vietnam
P.w: An 8-hectare riverside ecotourism park on a former Sác-forest island in Nhơn Trạch, ~30 km from HCMC — river swimming and boat rides, team-building and camping, and rustic local dishes (clay-pot chicken, grilled snakehead). Nominated among Vietnam's top-7 impressive eco-resorts in 2024.

P.n: Làng Nổi Tân Lập (Tân Lập Floating Village)
P.ad: Xã Tân Lập, huyện Mộc Hóa, Long An, Vietnam
P.w: A flooded Melaleuca (tràm) forest reserve ~100 km from Saigon and the marquee nature stop in Long An. A metre-wide concrete path winds ~5 km straight through the cajuput canopy over the water, with a 38 m, 10-storey observation tower over the Đồng Tháp Mười wetlands; explore by rowboat among lotus, water lilies and wild rice. Flood season (roughly Aug–Nov) is peak.

P.n: Chợ Nổi Cái Bè (Cái Bè Floating Market) — CLOSED
P.ad: Thị trấn Cái Bè, huyện Cái Bè, Tiền Giang, Vietnam
P.w: One of the Mekong Delta's great floating markets, trading on the Tiền River since the 17th–18th centuries and, by the 19th, a major wholesale hub for rice, dried fish and fruit — each boat hanging its wares from a 'cây bẹo' pole. It sits at the junction of Tiền Giang, Vĩnh Long and Đồng Tháp; go at dawn, and note it has thinned in recent years as road transport rose.

P.n: Cồn Phụng & the Đạo Dừa Relic (Phoenix Islet)
P.ad: Xã Tân Thạch, huyện Châu Thành, Bến Tre, Vietnam
P.w: A Tiền-River islet — one of the delta's 'four sacred islets' (Long–Lân–Quy–Phụng) — that is Bến Tre's classic day-trip: coconut-candy workshops, honey-tea gardens, horse-cart rides and boat runs through coconut-palm creeks. At its heart is the surreal relic of the 'Coconut Religion' (Đạo Dừa) founded by France-trained engineer-monk Nguyễn Thành Nam in 1963, with a nine-dragon plaza and octagonal Cửu Trùng Đài tower.

P.n: Nhà Cổ Huỳnh Thủy Lê (Huỳnh Thủy Lê Ancient House)
P.ad: 255A Nguyễn Huệ, Phường 2, TP. Sa Đéc, Đồng Tháp, Vietnam
P.w: An 1895 merchant house — French shell, Chinese-Vietnamese interior — that belonged to Huỳnh Thủy Lê, the wealthy young Chinese man whose teenage affair with Marguerite Duras became her Goncourt-winning novel 'The Lover' (L'Amant), filmed by Jean-Jacques Annaud in 1992. A national relic and Sa Đéc's most-visited sight; you can even stay overnight.

P.n: Làng Hoa Sa Đéc (Sa Đéc Flower Village, Tân Quy Đông)
P.ad: Phường Tân Quy Đông, TP. Sa Đéc, Đồng Tháp, Vietnam
P.w: The largest flower-and-ornamental-plant village in the country and the Mekong's Tết-bloom capital — a century-old craft village on the Tiền River raising 2,000+ species across hundreds of hectares, growers tending beds on stilts and by boat. Most photogenic in the weeks before Lunar New Year and during the Sa Đéc flower festival.

P.n: Làng Nghề Bột Sa Đéc (Sa Đéc Rice-Flour Village)
P.ad: Xã Tân Phú Đông & Phường 2, TP. Sa Đéc, Đồng Tháp, Vietnam
P.w: The century-old rice-flour craft village strung along the Ngã Bát River whose exceptionally white, fine, non-sour flour is the reason hủ tiếu Sa Đéc tastes the way it does — supplying noodle and cake makers across the south. A working glimpse of the delta's food supply chain behind the region's famous noodles.

P.n: Làng Gạch Gốm Mang Thít (Mang Thít Brick & Pottery Kilns)
P.ad: Huyện Mang Thít, Vĩnh Long, Vietnam
P.w: Vĩnh Long's 'Kingdom of Red Kilns' — a 200-year brick-tile-and-pottery landscape of domed beehive kilns clustered along the Thầy Cai canal to the Cổ Chiên River. Once the delta's biggest brick centre with 3,000+ kilns, now around 800 survive and are being conserved as a 'contemporary heritage' site; the weathered red domes make it one of the delta's most striking places to wander and shoot.

P.n: Nhà Cổ Bình Thủy (Bình Thủy Ancient House)
P.ad: 142-144 Bùi Hữu Nghĩa, P. Bình Thủy, Cần Thơ, Vietnam
P.w: The finest ancient house in Cần Thơ — the Dương family's five-chamber mansion, first built 1870 and completed in its current Indochine form by 1911, fusing French and Vietnamese-Chinese detail with imported European tiles and ironwork. A national architectural-historical relic (2009) and a film set (it appeared in 'The Lover').

P.n: Chùa Ông Cần Thơ (Quảng Triệu Hội Quán)
P.ad: 32 Hai Bà Trưng, Ninh Kiều, Cần Thơ, Vietnam
P.w: A vivid Cantonese assembly hall on the Hậu-River waterfront by Ninh Kiều, built 1894–1896 by Guangdong migrants from Guangzhou and Zhaoqing and dedicated to Quan Cong. Ranked a national historical-architectural relic in 1993, its coiled-dragon roof, incense spirals and red-and-gold interior make it central Cần Thơ's most atmospheric temple.

P.ad: Quốc lộ 1, nối Cần Thơ với Vĩnh Long (sông Hậu), Cần Thơ, Vietnam
P.w: The great cable-stayed bridge over the Hậu River linking Cần Thơ to Vĩnh Long. On completion in 2010 its 550 m main span was the longest of any cable-stayed bridge in Southeast Asia, ending generations of ferry crossings on National Highway 1 into the western delta — a landmark best seen lit at night from Ninh Kiều.

P.n: Cồn Sơn (Con Son Island Community Tourism)
P.ad: P. Bùi Hữu Nghĩa, quận Bình Thủy, Cồn Sơn, Cần Thơ, Vietnam
P.w: A 70-ha orchard islet mid-Hậu-River where ~30 farming households run a genuine community-tourism cooperative: visit floating fish rafts, make folk cakes with local families, pick fruit, and watch the famous 'flying snakehead fish' leap in formation to be fed. A slower, hands-on alternative to the standard floating-market run, reached by short boat hop from Bình Thủy.

P.ad: 118 Nguyen Van Thu, Dakao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: Ho Chi Minh City's leading contemporary commercial gallery (founded 2003), a four-floor 600 sqm space showing serious Vietnamese and international artists. The best single stop to gauge the city's contemporary art scene; Tue-Sat, free.

P.ad: 6D Ngo Thoi Nhiem, Ward 7, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A heritage-and-arts house-museum in a historic District 3 villa, founded by collector John Tue Nguyen as a hub for Vietnamese art and culture with a specialist library. Exhibitions plus salon events; Tuesdays open, other days by appointment.

P.ad: 27i Tran Nhat Duat, Tan Dinh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: One of Saigon's longest-running commercial galleries (est. 2009), known for championing emerging and mid-career Vietnamese painters. A reliable window on contemporary local painting away from the tourist trail.

P.ad: 48/7 Me Linh, Ward 19, Binh Thanh District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: Vietnam's most influential artist-run nonprofit (founded 2007 by Dinh Q Le and others), running exhibitions, talks and a residency program. The intellectual engine of the country's independent contemporary art; check current location/programming before visiting as it relocates periodically.

P.ad: 1057 Binh Quoi, Ward 28, Binh Thanh District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: An artist-run experimental art space on the leafy Binh Quoi peninsula, hosting installations, performances, sound events and open studios. A destination for the city's more avant-garde, non-commercial art.

P.ad: 15 Nguyen U Di, Thao Dien Ward, District 2 (Thu Duc City), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: Vietnam's first purpose-built independent contemporary arts centre (opened 2016 in Thao Dien), with gallery halls, a cafe/bar and design shop. The anchor of the Thao Dien art cluster; confirm current programming/hours before going.

P.n: Ao Dai Museum (Bao Tang Ao Dai)
P.ad: 206/19/30 Long Thuan, Long Phuoc Ward, District 9 (Thu Duc City), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A garden-house museum by designer Si Hoang tracing the evolution of Vietnam's national dress, the ao dai, through centuries of examples. A tranquil riverside garden setting ~22 km east of the centre; daily 09:00-18:00, ~100,000d.

P.ad: 870 Truong Sa, Ward 14, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A near-century-old pagoda on the Nhieu Loc Canal, a city-designated heritage site and the city's most photogenic Vesak venue, when thousands of lanterns are floated on the water. Serene canal-side visit any day; spectacular at Buddha's Birthday (4th lunar month).

P.ad: 1408 Duong 3 Thang 2, Ward 2, District 11, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: An early-19th-century pagoda built on the foundations of an ancient Khmer/Oc Eo-era temple mound, a recognised National Historical-Cultural Monument with a fine timber-framed Southern-style hall. A quiet, deeply historic stop in District 11.

P.ad: 161/85/20 Lac Long Quan, Ward 3, District 11, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A 1789 pagoda (sister to Giac Lam) once patronised by Emperor Gia Long, a National Historical-Cultural Relic preserving over 150 antique statues and classic Southern Vietnamese temple carving. Atmospheric and rarely crowded, tucked beside Dam Sen.

P.ad: 120 Tran Binh Trong, Ward 2, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: The oldest Catholic parish in the city (origins to 1722; present Gothic-Revival church inaugurated 1896), with soaring stone columns, red-tile roof and a climbable bell tower. A monumental, little-touristed church in the Cho Lon area.

P.ad: Pham Ngu Lao, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A long, 9-hectare downtown green ribbon on the site of Saigon's demolished 19th-century railway station, running from behind Ben Thanh Market through the backpacker quarter. Handy central breathing space for a stroll or people-watching.

P.ad: Dien Bien Phu, Da Kao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A shaded central park laid out in 1983 over the former Massiges (European) Cemetery, once the resting place of colonial elites and President Ngo Dinh Diem. A leafy escape with a fascinating buried history documented by Saigoneer.

P.ad: 10B Ton Duc Thang, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: The 1.3 km riverside park and pier on the Saigon River where locals gather at sunset and river cruises and the 15,000d public waterbus depart for Thu Duc. The best way to see the city from the water, past Landmark 81 and Bitexco.

P.ad: 141 Bach Dang, Ward 2, Binh Thanh District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A sprawling 1942 wet-and-wares market that is the beating heart of Binh Thanh, next to the Le Van Duyet tomb, with a lively street-food night market spilling out after dark. An authentic, tourist-light local market.

P.ad: 07 Cong Truong Lam Son, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: The signature 'bamboo circus' by Lune Production staged in the colonial Saigon Opera House, blending acrobatics, contemporary dance and live folk music into a rural-to-urban Vietnamese story. The city's marquee cultural show (~1 hour, nightly).

P.ad: 55B Nguyen Thi Minh Khai, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: The city's main venue for mua roi nuoc (water puppetry), the thousand-year-old northern folk art performed on a pool of water with live traditional musicians. Two short shows daily (17:00 and 18:30) beside Tao Dan Park.

P.ad: Le Cong Kieu, Nguyen Thai Binh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A 200 m lane near Ben Thanh (the former Rue de Reims) packed with dozens of antique and curio shops selling colonial memorabilia, old coins, ceramics, watches and reproductions. A browsable slice of old Saigon; haggle hard.

P.ad: 34-36 An Duong Vuong, Ward 9, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A 70-year-old, four-storey wholesale market on the edge of Cho Lon and the city's largest fashion bazaar, plus a famously good basement food court and dried-goods hall. Grittier and cheaper than Ben Thanh; a real trading experience.

P.n: Ton That Dam Old Market (Cho Cu)
P.ad: Ton That Dam, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: Saigon's original 'old market', a one-block street bazaar of produce, meat and liquor that was once the city's premier source of imported goods before Ben Thanh was built. A raw, fast-vanishing pocket of downtown history documented by Saigoneer.

P.n: Hai Thuong Lan Ong Traditional Medicine Street
P.ad: Hai Thuong Lan Ong, Ward 10, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A ~1 km Cho Lon street lined with 60-80 traditional-medicine shops, the oldest and largest herbal district in the city, its air thick with cinnamon, star anise, ginseng and dried herbs. A sensory heritage walk named for the father of Vietnamese medicine.

P.ad: 14 Ton That Dam, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A gritty, atmospheric old apartment block (the original 'cafe apartment', predating the famous 42 Nguyen Hue one) whose maze of corridors hides cool cafes, hipster bars and boutiques. A raw, architecturally fascinating dive into old-Saigon apartment life.

P.ad: Le Thanh Ton & Thai Van Lung, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A compact 'Little Tokyo' of lantern-hung alleys around Le Thanh Ton and Thai Van Lung, home to 300+ Japanese expats and a dense cluster of izakayas, ramen shops and karaoke bars. A miniature Japan in the heart of District 1, best after dark.

P.ad: 66 Ton That Thiep, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A colourful late-19th-century Hindu temple built by Saigon's Tamil community and dedicated to Lord Murugan, one of only three Hindu temples left in the city. A vivid, incense-filled surprise on a quiet downtown lane.

P.ad: 116A Hung Vuong, Ward 9, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A twin-spired Gothic church built 1922-1928 at the Nga Sau six-way roundabout, one of the city's most ornate ecclesiastical buildings and among the largest churches in Cho Lon. A striking, off-circuit alternative to Notre-Dame.

P.ad: 132-134 Dong Khoi, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: The city's oldest hotel (1880) on former Rue Catinat opposite the Opera House, where Graham Greene wrote much of 'The Quiet American' in Room 214 and its terrace was the correspondents' 1950s watering hole. A living piece of literary and war-era Saigon.

P.ad: 01 Dong Khoi, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A 1925 French-colonial landmark on the Dong Khoi/Ton Duc Thang riverfront corner, built by the tycoon Hui Bon Hoa and preserving its original Art Deco character. Worth a look for the facade and a drink at its river-view rooftop.

P.ad: 141 Nguyen Hue, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: The open-air rooftop bar of the 1960 Rex Hotel, site of the US military's daily wartime press briefings mocked as the 'Five O'Clock Follies'. Iconic Vietnam-War history plus sweeping views over Nguyen Hue and City Hall.

P.ad: 65 Le Loi, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: The city's most polished shopping complex on Le Loi, anchored by Vietnam's first Takashimaya Japanese department store with a top-floor food court and basement Japanese supermarket. A cool, glossy contrast to the street markets.

P.ad: 3 Hoa Binh, Ward 3, District 11, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: A 50-hectare cultural-and-amusement park in District 11 with landscaped gardens, thrill rides, cultural exhibits and an adjoining water park. One of the city's big family day-outs, alongside Suoi Tien and Dai Nam.

P.ad: BB4, 188 Nguyen Van Huong, Thao Dien Ward, District 2 (Thu Duc City), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: The live-jazz club of celebrated saxophonist Tran Manh Tuan, blending fusion and traditional jazz with Vietnamese folk influences; nightly sets from ~21:00. Recently relocated from downtown to Thao Dien; the city's premier jazz institution.

P.ad: Kuala Lumpur City Centre (KLCC), Jalan Ampang, Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
P.w: The 452 m twin towers with the double-decker skybridge — KL's defining landmark, once the world's tallest buildings.

P.ad: Gombak, Selangor (Greater Kuala Lumpur), Malaysia
P.w: A limestone hill of Hindu cave temples reached by 272 rainbow steps under the giant golden Murugan statue; focus of the Thaipusam festival.

P.ad: George Town, Penang, Malaysia
P.w: The UNESCO-listed old town of clan jetties, shophouses, temples and the famous street-art murals (part of 'Melaka and George Town, Historic Cities of the Straits of Malacca').

P.ad: Air Itam, Penang, Malaysia
P.w: Southeast Asia's largest Chinese Buddhist temple, with the Pagoda of Ten Thousand Buddhas and a 30 m bronze Kuan Yin.

P.n: Cheong Fatt Tze — The Blue Mansion
P.ad: 14 Leith Street, George Town, Penang, Malaysia
P.w: The indigo-blue Hakka merchant mansion, a multi-award-winning heritage restoration and film location ('Crazy Rich Asians').

P.ad: Bandar Hilir, Malacca (Melaka), Malaysia
P.w: The 1511 Portuguese fort gate (Porta de Santiago), the red Dutch Stadthuys/Christ Church and Jonker Street — the heart of UNESCO Malacca.

P.ad: Na Phra Lan Road, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok, Thailand
P.w: The 1782 royal palace complex and the Temple of the Emerald Buddha — Thailand's most sacred and most-visited site.

P.ad: 158 Thanon Wang Doem, Bangkok Yai, Bangkok, Thailand
P.w: The Temple of Dawn, its porcelain-encrusted riverside prang rising over the Chao Phraya.

P.ad: 2 Sanam Chai Road, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok, Thailand
P.w: Home of the 46 m gold-leafed Reclining Buddha and the birthplace of traditional Thai massage.

P.ad: 587/10 Kamphaeng Phet 2 Road, Chatuchak, Bangkok, Thailand
P.w: One of the world's largest weekend markets — 15,000+ stalls of food, crafts, plants and vintage.

P.ad: Doi Suthep, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, Thailand
P.w: The gold-chedi mountain temple above Chiang Mai, reached by a 300-step naga staircase — the city's emblem.

P.n: Chiang Mai Old City Temples (Wat Chedi Luang & Wat Phra Singh)
P.ad: Old City (within the moat), Chiang Mai, Thailand
P.w: The walled Old City's Lanna temples — the ruined 14th-century Chedi Luang and the revered Wat Phra Singh.

P.ad: 28 Vo Van Tan Street, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: HCMC's unflinching museum of the Indochina and Vietnam wars — the city's most affecting historical site.

P.ad: Le Loi, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: The landmark 1914 central market — street food, textiles and souvenirs in the heart of Saigon.

P.ad: Cu Chi District (Ben Dinh / Ben Duoc), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
P.w: The vast wartime underground tunnel network northwest of the city — a defining day trip from Saigon.

P.n: Hoan Kiem Lake, Ngoc Son Temple & the Old Quarter
P.ad: Hoan Kiem District, Hanoi, Vietnam
P.w: Hanoi's civic heart — the legendary lake and its red bridge to Ngoc Son Temple, ringed by the 36-streets Old Quarter.

P.ad: Quang Ninh Province (day trip / cruise from Hanoi), Vietnam
P.w: The UNESCO seascape of thousands of limestone karst islands — Vietnam's iconic natural wonder.

P.ad: Hoi An, Quang Nam Province, Vietnam
P.w: The UNESCO-listed trading port of lantern-lit streets, Japanese Covered Bridge and preserved merchant houses.

P.ad: Magelang Regency (near Yogyakarta), Central Java, Indonesia
P.w: The world's largest Buddhist temple, a 9th-century stupa-mountain of 2,600+ relief panels — UNESCO World Heritage.

P.ad: Sleman (Yogyakarta–Central Java border), Indonesia
P.w: Indonesia's largest Hindu temple compound, a soaring 9th-century Shiva complex — UNESCO World Heritage.

P.ad: Pecatu, South Kuta, Bali, Indonesia
P.w: A sea temple perched on a 70 m cliff above the Indian Ocean, famous for sunset and the kecak fire dance.

P.ad: Beraban, Kediri, Tabanan, Bali, Indonesia
P.w: The much-photographed sea temple on a tidal rock offshore — Bali's classic sunset silhouette.

P.ad: Tegallalang, north of Ubud, Bali, Indonesia
P.w: The emerald stepped paddies of the subak system — part of Bali's only UNESCO site, the Cultural Landscape of Bali Province.

P.ad: West Jakarta, Jakarta, Indonesia
P.w: The Dutch-colonial old town around Fatahillah Square, with the Jakarta History Museum and Cafe Batavia.

P.ad: Intramuros, Manila, Philippines
P.w: The 16th-century Spanish walled city — cobbled streets, bastions and Fort Santiago, the historic core of Manila.

P.ad: General Luna Street, Intramuros, Manila, Philippines
P.w: The oldest stone church in the Philippines (1607) and a UNESCO 'Baroque Churches of the Philippines' World Heritage site.

P.ad: Ermita, Manila, Philippines
P.w: The historic seaside park at the site of national hero Jose Rizal's execution, marked by the Rizal Monument.

P.n: Basilica Minore del Santo Nino & Magellan's Cross
P.ad: Osmena Boulevard / P. Burgos Street, Cebu City, Philippines
P.w: The country's oldest Catholic relic and church, beside the 1521 cross planted at Magellan's arrival — the cradle of Philippine Christianity.

P.ad: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap, Cambodia
P.w: The largest religious monument on earth, the 12th-century Khmer temple-city and Cambodia's national symbol — UNESCO World Heritage.

P.ad: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap, Cambodia
P.w: The walled royal city of Angkor Thom and the Bayon's forest of giant serene stone faces.

P.ad: Sothearos Boulevard, Phnom Penh, Cambodia
P.w: The Khmer royal palace complex on the riverfront, including the Silver Pagoda with its emerald and gold Buddhas.

P.n: Luang Prabang Old Town (Wat Xieng Thong)
P.ad: Luang Prabang peninsula, Laos
P.w: The UNESCO-listed royal town where Lao and French-colonial architecture meet, crowned by the 1560 Wat Xieng Thong and the dawn alms-giving.

P.ad: ~29 km south of Luang Prabang, Laos
P.w: Turquoise multi-tiered travertine waterfalls in the jungle — Luang Prabang's signature natural excursion.

P.ad: Singuttara Hill, Yangon, Myanmar
P.w: Myanmar's most sacred Buddhist site — a 112 m gold-plated stupa said to enshrine relics of the Buddha.

P.ad: Bagan, Mandalay Region, Myanmar
P.w: A plain studded with thousands of 11th–13th-century Buddhist temples and pagodas — UNESCO World Heritage.

P.ad: 18 Marina Gardens Drive, Marina Bay
P.w: Waterfront nature park with the Supertree Grove, Cloud Forest & Flower Dome; over 1.5 million plants.

P.n: Marina Bay Sands SkyPark Observation Deck
P.ad: 10 Bayfront Avenue, Marina Bay
P.w: The 57th-storey deck atop Marina Bay Sands' three towers, with panoramic skyline views over the bay.

P.ad: 1 Fullerton Road, Marina Bay
P.w: Home of the 8.6 m Merlion, Singapore's lion-headed, fish-bodied national symbol, spouting into the bay.

P.ad: 6 Bayfront Avenue, Marina Bay
P.w: Lotus-shaped museum at Marina Bay Sands; home to the teamLab 'Future World' digital art gallery.

P.ad: 30 Raffles Avenue, Marina Bay
P.w: A 165 m observation wheel over Marina Bay with views to the city, the Straits and beyond.

P.ad: 1 St Andrew's Road, Civic District
P.w: World's largest public collection of Singapore & Southeast Asian art, in the former City Hall & Supreme Court.

P.ad: 93 Stamford Road, Civic District
P.w: The nation's oldest museum (est. 1849), narrating Singapore's social history.

P.ad: 1 Empress Place, Civic District
P.w: Riverside museum devoted to the material cultures of Asia, from Chinese to West Asian civilisations.

P.ad: 1 Beach Road, Civic District
P.w: 1887 colonial-era grande dame; a National Monument and birthplace of the Singapore Sling.

P.ad: River Valley Road, Fort Canning
P.w: Historic hilltop park with artefacts dating to the 1300s; the famous Fort Canning tree tunnel.

P.ad: 1 Esplanade Drive, Marina Bay
P.w: The 'durian' performing-arts centre on the bayfront, a defining piece of the skyline.

P.ad: 244 South Bridge Road, Chinatown
P.w: Singapore's oldest Hindu temple (1827); a National Monument with a vivid gopuram tower.

P.ad: 288 South Bridge Road, Chinatown
P.w: Tang-style Buddhist temple (2007) housing a sacred tooth relic in a 3,500 kg gold stupa.

P.ad: 158 Telok Ayer Street, Chinatown
P.w: Singapore's oldest Hokkien temple (1839) dedicated to Mazu; a National Monument built without nails.

P.ad: 48 Pagoda Street, Chinatown
P.w: Recreated 1950s shophouse interiors telling the story of Chinatown's early immigrant tenants.

P.ad: 3 Muscat Street, Kampong Glam
P.w: Kampong Glam's golden-domed royal mosque; a National Monument and the heart of the Malay-Arab quarter.

P.ad: 141 Serangoon Road, Little India
P.w: Little India's landmark Hindu temple to the goddess Kali, founded by Tamil lime-kiln workers (1855).

P.n: Former House of Tan Teng Niah
P.ad: 37 Kerbau Road, Little India
P.w: The last surviving Chinese villa in Little India (1900), painted in vivid rainbow colours.

P.n: Koon Seng Road Peranakan Shophouses (Joo Chiat/Katong)
P.ad: Koon Seng Road, Joo Chiat
P.w: Singapore's most photographed row of pastel Peranakan shophouses (1920s) in the Katong-Joo Chiat conservation area.

P.n: Jewel Changi Airport & HSBC Rain Vortex
P.ad: 78 Airport Boulevard, Changi Airport
P.w: Glass-domed nature-and-retail complex housing the world's tallest indoor waterfall (40 m) and Shiseido Forest Valley.

P.ad: 1000 Upper Changi Road North, Changi
P.w: NHB museum commemorating WWII POWs interned at Changi, with a replica of the Changi Chapel.

P.ad: East Coast Park Service Road, Marine Parade
P.w: Singapore's largest seaside park; 15 km of coastline for cycling, seafood and the sea breeze.

P.ad: 1 Geylang Serai
P.w: The cultural heart of the Malay-Muslim community; a bustling wet market and Ramadan bazaar hub.

P.ad: 1 Cluny Road, Bukit Timah
P.w: Singapore's first UNESCO World Heritage Site (2015); a 160-year-old tropical garden with the National Orchid Garden.

P.ad: Henderson Road, Mount Faber / Telok Blangah
P.w: 10 km of ridge-top trails linking Mount Faber, Telok Blangah & Kent Ridge, crossing the wave-form Henderson Waves, Singapore's highest pedestrian bridge.

P.ad: 262 Pasir Panjang Road
P.w: 1937 cultural theme park (ex-Tiger Balm Garden) of surreal dioramas, famed for the Ten Courts of Hell.

P.ad: MacRitchie Reservoir Park, Lornie Road
P.w: Central Catchment rainforest reservoir with a 250 m suspension bridge, 25 m up in the forest canopy.

P.ad: 177 Hindhede Drive, Bukit Timah
P.w: ASEAN Heritage Park protecting primary rainforest and Singapore's highest natural point (163 m).

P.ad: 80 Mandai Lake Road, Mandai
P.w: World-renowned open-concept zoo of over 4,200 animals in naturalistic, cage-free habitats.

P.ad: 80 Mandai Lake Road, Mandai
P.w: The world's first nocturnal zoo (1994); tram rides through 35 hectares of after-dark habitats.

P.ad: 80 Mandai Lake Road, Mandai
P.w: Asia's only river-themed wildlife park, home to giant pandas and a giant Amazon river tank.

P.ad: Lorong Mambong, Holland Village
P.w: A long-time bohemian expat enclave of eateries, bars and shophouses off Holland Road.

P.ad: Lorong 6 Toa Payoh (in front of Blk 28), Singapore
P.w: Singapore's most iconic surviving 1979 mosaic 'dragon' playground, designed by HDB's Khor Ean Ghee — a terrazzo-tiled dragon head with a climbable ring body. One of only two dragon playgrounds left and a marquee stop on NHB's Toa Payoh Heritage Trail.

P.ad: 184 Jalan Toa Payoh, Singapore 319944
P.w: Singapore's oldest Buddhist monastery — completed 1909 and gazetted a National Monument in 1980 — modelled on Fuzhou's Xi Chan Monastery, with the Hall of Celestial Kings and Mahavira Hall laid out in the classic cong lin ('layered forest') plan.

P.n: Toa Payoh Town Park & Look-Out Tower
P.ad: Lorong 6 Toa Payoh (beside Toa Payoh HDB Hub), Singapore
P.w: The 4.8-hectare 1970s town park that pioneered greenery in HDB new towns — landscaped ponds, rustic gazebos and the conserved 25 m space-age Look-Out Tower, a favourite 1970s-80s wedding-photo backdrop.
P.k: Open daily, free; tower not accessible

P.ad: 91 Toa Payoh Central, Singapore 319193
P.w: Toa Payoh's first Catholic church (inaugurated 1971), a modernist landmark at the junction of Toa Payoh Central and Lorong 4 that has long offered Mass in English, Mandarin and Tamil — featured on the Toa Payoh Heritage Trail's 'Of Faiths & Beliefs' route.

P.ad: 53 Lorong 5 Toa Payoh, Singapore 310053
P.w: The Y-shaped 1967 HDB showpiece with a rooftop viewing gallery once used to survey the young new town from above. Queen Elizabeth II visited in 1972 (as did Princess Anne, Prince Philip and other dignitaries), earning it the 'VIP Block' name.
P.k: Rooftop gallery closed; view from ground level

P.ad: 480 Lorong 6 Toa Payoh, Singapore 310480
P.w: HDB's headquarters and the civic heart of Singapore's first fully HDB-built satellite town, home to relocated public sculptures — Ng Eng Teng's 'The Climb', Chong Fah Cheong's 'Mama's Precious One' and Ju Ming's 'Tai Chi Boxing' — plus a mall, library and hawker fare.

P.ad: Toa Payoh Central (trail starts near HDB Hub), Singapore
P.w: NHB's self-guided trail through Singapore's second satellite town, linking 16-plus sites — from the Dragon Playground and Town Park to Shuang Lin Monastery — across two themed routes, 'Of Public Housing & Shared Spaces' and 'Of Faiths & Beliefs'.

P.n: United Temple (United Five Temples of Toa Payoh)
P.ad: Lorong 6 Toa Payoh (near Blk 177/178), Singapore
P.w: Established 1974, the first temple in Singapore to house smaller constituent temples under one roof — five village temples (Chee Tian Keng, Shan Zu Yuan Fu De Ci, Tong Xing Gang, Zhao Ying Ci and others) that were displaced when Toa Payoh's kampongs were cleared pooled their devotees' funds to build here. A landmark on NHB's Toa Payoh Heritage Trail 'Of Faiths & Beliefs' route.

P.ad: 2001 Lorong 8 Toa Payoh, Singapore 319259
P.w: A Dravidian-style Hindu temple to the goddess Kaliamman, tracing to an 1860 shrine near Orchard Road and rebuilt at Toa Payoh in 1982 (consecrated 1986). Notable for founding Saraswathi Kindergarten, said to be Singapore's first pre-school, and a stop on the Toa Payoh Heritage Trail's 'Of Faiths & Beliefs' route.

P.ad: Lorong 5 / Lorong 6 Toa Payoh, Singapore
P.w: Singapore's first sensory park (opened 2009), a 1.1-hectare garden by Surbana and Yoshisuke Miyake split into five zones for sight, smell, touch, sound and taste — with larger-than-life optical-illusion mirrors that reveal a hidden face, resonating steel 'drum' plates, a playground and a fragrant garden.

P.ad: 6 Toa Payoh Central, Singapore 319191
P.w: Inaugurated 7 Feb 1974, the second public library of the 1970s branch-building drive and a civic anchor of the town — its Children's Section riffs on the iconic dragon playground with hexagonal mosaic-tile motifs. A pioneering heartland library documented in NLB's BiblioAsia.
P.k: Free; closed Mondays historically — check hours

P.n: Toa Payoh Seu Teck Sean Tong
P.ad: 15 Lorong 6 Toa Payoh (Kampong Hup Choon Hng site), Singapore
P.w: A Chinese charitable temple established as an attap hut in 1942 and rebuilt 1959, enshrining the deity Song Da Feng and blending Buddhist, Taoist and Confucian rites. Its medical wing (opened 1967) still gives free Traditional Chinese Medicine consultations — a living community institution on the heritage trail.

P.ad: Toa Payoh MRT Station (NS19), 480 Lorong 6 Toa Payoh, Singapore
P.w: A station wall mural in SMRT's heritage-mural series telling Toa Payoh's story as the first town wholly designed and built by the HDB — co-created by James Suresh, better known as co-creator of the 'Mr Kiasu' comics. A quick, free public-art stop right at the interchange.

P.ad: 293 Toa Payoh Lorong 6, Singapore 319387
P.w: The town's big community-and-sports clubhouse (open to the public, not just NSmen) with a leisure pool and lap lanes, bowling, badminton, tennis, gym, karaoke and F&B — the recreation hub that carries on locally while the adjacent old stadium and swimming complex are redeveloped into the Toa Payoh Integrated Development.

F.ad: 288 Nam Ky Khoi Nghia (in the alley), Vo Thi Sau Ward, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Legendary 60-year alley phở serving strict Nam Dinh/Northern-style beef phở with no herbs, sprouts or hoisin - the 'take it or leave it' bowl locals queue for.

F.ad: 435 Ly Thai To, Ward 9, District 10, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: North-to-South phở institution since 1954, famed for its giant 'to xe lua' (train-car) bowl of simple, garnish-free Northern phở bac that Saigonese have loved for 70+ years.

F.ad: 25 Mac Dinh Chi, Da Kao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: One of Saigon's oldest phở houses, founded 1947 by Mr Tran Van Phon and still simmering its crystal-clear, lightly sweet broth over a charcoal stove; now second/third generation.

F.ad: 380 Nguyen Tri Phuong, Ward 6, District 10, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: The standout of District 10's neon-lit chè Thái street; a famously rich Thai-style sweet soup of pureed durian, jackfruit, palm seed and longan in coconut milk.

F.ad: Huynh Man Dat, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Cholon hủ tiếu Nam Vang run by a former cook for the Khmer royal family - one of the few places serving genuinely Cambodian-style Phnom Penh noodles in Saigon.

F.ad: Vo Van Tan, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: One of Saigon's most storied hủ tiếu Nam Vang brands and reputedly its most expensive bowl - Chinese-Cambodian noodles with minced pork, liver, heart, shrimp and quail egg in a refined sweet broth.

F.ad: 113A Dang Dung, Tan Dinh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: The 'Commando Cafe' - a 1940s house that was a secret Viet Cong special-forces base with a weapons bunker and hidden mailbox; today it pours nostalgic bac xiu and serves com tam Dai Han above its wartime tunnel.

F.ad: 207B Nguyen Van Thu, Da Kao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A perennially packed bún bò Huế spot beside the Conservatory of Music, singled out by a visiting New York chef as one of the best bowls of soup in all of Vietnam.

F.n: Banh Khot Co Ba Vung Tau
F.ad: 40B Tran Cao Van, Ward 6, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Saigon's best-known outpost of Vung Tau-style banh khot - crispy coconut-batter mini rice pancakes topped with shrimp - wrapped with herbs and dipped in sweet fish sauce; also serves banh xeo.

F.ad: 277 Vo Van Tan, Ward 5, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A 40-year Chinese-Vietnamese street stall whose bot chien - rice-flour cake pan-fried crisp in a copper pan with egg, scallion and rich soy - is a Saigon late-afternoon institution.

F.ad: 25 Hoang Sa, Da Kao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Canalside beef pho stall; MICHELIN Bib Gourmand 2024-2026, famed for its long-braised oxtail.

F.ad: 63/6 Pasteur, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Alley pho institution serving Saigonese since 1945; MICHELIN Bib Gourmand, pairs its broth with pate chaud.

F.ad: 260C Pasteur, Ward 8, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Landmark Southern pho since 1968; MICHELIN Bib Gourmand, a whole plate of herbs, bean sprouts and you tiao.

F.ad: 413-415 Nguyen Trai, Ward 7, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Cholon-area pho household name since 1970; generous flank-and-filet bowls, in the MICHELIN Guide selection.

F.ad: 460 Nguyen Tri Phuong, Ward 9, District 10, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: MICHELIN Bib Gourmand pho whose owner simmers a clear beef broth over 12 hours; customizable cuts.

F.ad: 148 Vo Thi Sau, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Humble pho ga stall since 1958 in the MICHELIN Guide; freshly-made clear chicken broth, second generation.

F.ad: 19 Huynh Khuong Ninh, Da Kao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Nearly-century-old banh mi cart (est. 1930), now third generation, with homemade pate and pork roll.

F.ad: 53 Cao Thang, Ward 3, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Iconic 1958 breakfast spot; sizzling cast-iron skillet of fried eggs, pate and cold cuts with baguette.

F.ad: 37-39 Nguyen Trai, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Alley cart open ~4 hours a day; sweet charcoal-grilled pork patties in place of pate, a Saigon street icon.

F.ad: 14B Street 46, Ward 2, District 4, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: The only bun bo Hue stall with a MICHELIN Bib Gourmand; a spicy, lemongrass-lifted broth with beef and tendon.

F.ad: Vo Van Tan, Ban Co Ward, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Chinese-Khmer-Vietnamese hu tieu Nam Vang since 1975; MICHELIN Bib Gourmand celebrated for its Phnom Penh-style bowl.

F.ad: 46A Dinh Cong Trang, Tan Dinh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Seven-decade banh xeo address opposite the Pink Church; charcoal-cooked crepes, MICHELIN Bib Gourmand, Bourdain-featured.

F.ad: 89 Ton That Dam, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Chef Peter Cuong Franklin's MICHELIN-starred restaurant over the Ton That Dam market; street food reimagined as fine dining.

F.ad: 136/9 Le Thanh Ton (Hem 136), Ben Thanh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Hole-in-the-wall down an alley by Ben Thanh's north gate; MICHELIN Bib Gourmand home cooking and shrimp banh xeo.

F.ad: 127 Dinh Tien Hoang, Da Kao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: MICHELIN Bib Gourmand banh cuon shop; freshly-made, paper-thin steamed rolls with pork and mushroom.

F.ad: 175C Co Giang, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: 40-year institution; sweet-sticky grilled pork soaked in nuoc cham, with nem nuong and shredded pork skin.

F.n: Banh Canh Cua 87 Tran Khac Chan
F.ad: 87 Tran Khac Chan, Tan Dinh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Corner stall famed for a thick, stew-like crab banh canh loaded with crab meat, crab cake and quail egg.

F.ad: 212B Alley, Nguyen Trai, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Saigon's most famous snail operation tucked down a downtown alley; 100+ snail and shellfish dishes.

F.ad: 42 Nguyen Hue, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: 1960s apartment block on the Nguyen Hue walking street turned vertical warren of 50+ cafes; a Saigon coffee landmark.

F.ad: 27 Ngo Duc Ke (2nd floor), Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Saigon's pioneering specialty-coffee roaster in a 1912 building; pour-over, cold brew and light-roast Arabica.

F.ad: 109/36 Nguyen Thien Thuat, Ward 2, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Saigon's oldest cafe (est. 1938), sole keeper of ca phe vot cloth-filter coffee, run by the founder's daughters.

F.ad: Ben Thanh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam (corner by Ben Thanh Market)
F.w: Nearly-70-year sticky-rice corner by Ben Thanh Market; MICHELIN Bib Gourmand xoi ga with house pate and quail egg.

F.ad: 718 Nguyen Dinh Chieu, Ward 1, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: One of Saigon's oldest che shops (since 1959); a spare menu of jasmine-scented sweet soups and white jelly.

F.ad: 10 Dang Tat, Tan Dinh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Beloved home-cooking restaurant in restored villas; MICHELIN Bib Gourmand, rice cooked in cast iron on wood stoves.

F.ad: 67 Ton That Dam, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Cantonese clay-pot rice shop since 1948, now third generation; MICHELIN Bib Gourmand for its double-boiled silkie soup.

F.ad: 129/4 Vo Van Tan, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Alley hideaway with a rooftop balcony; MICHELIN Bib Gourmand home cooking, signature oyster-and-beef hotpot.

F.ad: 15/20 Nguyen Thi Minh Khai, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Owner-run shop of generous Hanoian home cooking; MICHELIN Bib Gourmand bun rieu cua topped with crispy fried tofu.

F.ad: 55 Dong Du, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Always-busy Cantonese dim sum house by the Dong Du mosque; MICHELIN Bib Gourmand, a large dim sum and BBQ selection.

F.ad: Lot H, Ngo Gia Tu Apartment, Su Van Hanh, Ward 2, District 10, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Serving its legendary beef stew since 1975; MICHELIN Bib Gourmand bo kho with bread, noodles or rice.

F.ad: Xom Chieu Market, Ton Dan, District 4, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Cult late-night broken-rice stall (6pm-3am) behind Xom Chieu Market, made from 100% broken rice; a celebrity haunt.

F.ad: 163 Le Thanh Ton, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: 40-year bun rieu stall by Ben Thanh; a big fried-tofu, congealed-blood and giant crab-meatball bowl.

F.ad: 121 Co Giang, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Long-running Co Giang stall for smoky charcoal-grilled beef wrapped in la lot leaves, with noodles and nuoc cham.

F.ad: 59 Ho Xuan Huong, Ward 6, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Bourdain's 'flying rice': clay pots smashed and rice tossed across the room, from A Cook's Tour and No Reservations.

F.ad: 36 Le Loi (5th floor), Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Hidden rooftop above Le Loi serving northern Vietnamese home cooking with city views; part of the Cuc Gach/Secret Garden family.

F.ad: 167-169 Calmette, Nguyen Thai Binh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Marou's flagship cafe and bean-to-bar chocolate factory in a heritage building; award-winning single-origin Vietnamese cacao.

F.ad: 23 Hoang Sa, Da Kao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Nguyen Thi Thanh's canalside stall made famous by Bourdain's No Reservations; a different regional noodle soup each day.

F.ad: 136 Le Thanh Ton (1st floor), Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: 1960s-70s-styled cocktail bar on Asia's 50 Best Bars list; local-ingredient drinks like the sugarcane Nuoc Mia Highball.

F.ad: 25 Ho Tung Mau (2nd floor), Nguyen Thai Binh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Ingredient-focused hidden cocktail bar; debuted on Asia's 50 Best Bars (No.99, 2024) with drinks built on Vietnamese produce.

F.ad: 17-19 Ngo Van Nam, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Well-loved modern-traditional Vietnamese restaurant (since 2011); MSG-free home dishes in a vintage-contemporary setting.

F.ad: 110 Suong Nguyet Anh, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: MICHELIN Bib Gourmand modern-Vietnamese vegan kitchen using produce from the family garden; punchy bun Vi Que broth.

F.ad: 349-351 Nguyễn Trãi, Ward 7, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Hoa (Chinese-Vietnamese) noodle house going since the 1970s; the signature mì vịt tiềm pairs a lightly-fried, herb-braised duck leg with springy egg noodles in a thuốc-bắc broth, plus crisp fried wontons. A Chợ Lớn benchmark for the dish.

F.n: Hủ Tiếu Sa Tế Tô Ký
F.ad: Gia Phú, Ward 1, District 6, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Nearly-80-year-old Teochew family shop (founded by Tô Cẩm, now third generation) famous for hủ tiếu sa tế nai — a fiery, nutty satay broth built from 20-30 spices, peanuts and sesame poured over noodles with sliced venison. The reference for the dish in Chợ Lớn.

F.ad: 18 Cao Đạt, Ward 1, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A long-standing three-floor Chợ Lớn dim sum institution singled out by Michelin-recognised chef DoBee Lam as a favourite old-school điểm tâm hall — steamer carts of har gow, siu mai, cheung fun and Cantonese classics from morning.

F.n: Sủi Cảo Hà Tôn Quyền (Thiên Thiên)
F.ad: Hà Tôn Quyền, Ward 4, District 11, Cholon, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: The heart of Saigon's nicknamed 'phố sủi cảo' — a cluster of Hoa family dumpling shops (Thiên Thiên among the best-known) that have run for 30+ years each. Plump shrimp-and-pork sủi cảo steamed, fried, or in clear soup with handmade noodles.

F.ad: Chợ Phùng Hưng, Phùng Hưng, Ward 14, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A 70-year-old Hoa cà phê vợt (cloth-'sock'-filter coffee) stall tucked in Phùng Hưng market, roasting its own beans on site over wood with a touch of butter and salt. A living Cantonese coffee-culture relic of Chợ Lớn.

F.ad: Trần Hưng Đạo B, Ward 11, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: An ~80-year-old Cantonese dessert cart (opened 1938 by a Guangdong immigrant), nicknamed Chè Cột Điện and Chè Ma for its lamppost spot and late hours. Warm and iced Chinese sweet soups — almond, black-sesame, lotus and herbal chè — done the old way.

F.ad: Châu Văn Liêm, Ward 11, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A Chợ Lớn dumpling stalwart on Châu Văn Liêm known for chive-packed sủi cảo — soft-yet-chewy dumplings loaded with garlic-chive; also plates a Chinese-style phá lấu. A neighbourhood authority on the craft.

F.ad: 823 Nguyễn Trãi, Ward 14, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A 60-year, three-generation Teochew phá lấu cart on Nguyễn Trãi: pork ears, tongue, tripe, chicken feet and tofu braised in a five-spice, star-anise and cinnamon master stock, with a sweet Teochew dipping sauce. Also famed for its bánh mì phá lấu.

F.ad: 83 An Điềm, Ward 11, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A half-century-old Hoa dessert shop beloved by Chợ Lớn's Chinese community for nearly 30 gently-sweet Cantonese chè — almond tofu (đậu hũ hạnh nhân), steamed-egg custard, black sesame and egg tea. Opens late afternoon.

F.ad: Chợ Phùng Hưng, Phùng Hưng, Ward 14, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A rare taste of Chợ Lớn's Hakka (Hẹ) heritage: khổ qua cà ớt — bitter melon, chili and tomato stuffed with fish paste in a clear soup. A near-vanished home-style dish kept alive by a Phùng Hưng-market family stall.

F.ad: District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: An unassuming Chợ Lớn spot serving top-notch Taiwanese home-style comfort cooking — braises, rice bowls and hot soups — a Chinese-diaspora counterpoint to the Cantonese/Teochew canon around it.

F.n: Hủ Tiếu Bò Viên 153 Vĩnh Viễn
F.ad: 153 Vĩnh Viễn, Ward 4, District 10, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A ~1965 institution called one of Saigon's oldest beef-meatball noodle shops; hand-ground beef balls made fresh daily over an 8-hour beef-bone broth, a tight three-dish menu served afternoon to late night.

F.n: Cà Phê Vợt Hẻm 330 Phan Đình Phùng
F.ad: 330/2 Phan Đình Phùng, Ward 1, Phú Nhuận, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A French-era cloth-filter (cà phê vợt) coffee cart at the mouth of alley 330, run by octogenarians ông Ba and bà Ba; open around the clock, it has closed only once in over 60 years — Phú Nhuận's answer to Cheo Leo.

F.ad: Phan Xích Long (Phan Đăng Lưu to Vạn Kiếp), Ward 2, Phú Nhuận, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Phú Nhuận's official food street (launched Jan 2024): a 1.5km strip of 200+ eateries from Phan Đăng Lưu to Vạn Kiếp — hotpot, seafood, Thai, chè and café rows — one of the city's busiest night-dining destinations.

F.ad: 66/5 Lê Đại Hành, Ward 7, District 11, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A 70-plus-year Cantonese noodle house tucked in a Ward 7 alley (locals call it 'hẻm Tư Ky'), now in its third generation; the draw is hand-pulled mì made with duck egg and lye water, served as mì vịt tiềm and hoành thánh.

F.ad: 8 Hoàng Hoa Thám, Ward 7, Bình Thạnh, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
