F.w: A MICHELIN Bib Gourmand sticky-rice bar (opened 2021) — the only xôi specialist on the HCMC Bib list; signature xôi phá lấu trứng non tops sticky rice with braised offal, quail eggs and fried shallots, served with soup and kimchi.

F.ad: 52 Nguyễn Công Trứ, Ward 19, Bình Thạnh, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A 2026 MICHELIN Bib Gourmand phở shop in Bình Thạnh known for phở bắp hoa with medium-rare beef — and a viral 'phở tine' that plates beef-noodle broth with french fries and cheese.

F.ad: 57/21A Hồ Thị Kỷ, Ward 1, District 10, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A 50-plus-year Cambodian chè stall in the Hồ Thị Kỷ alley, run by Khmer-Vietnamese Cô Có (inherited from her mother); num-flan bí đỏ, palm-sugar coconut and sticky-rice Khmer sweets from ~7am, roughly 10–25k a bowl.

F.ad: 274/29 Võ Văn Tần, Ward 5, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Family-run bún bò Huế in a narrow District 3 alley; a MICHELIN Bib Gourmand for its rich lemongrass-and-beef-bone broth and generous mixed bowl.

F.ad: Nguyễn Thượng Hiền (Điện Biên Phủ to Nguyễn Đình Chiểu), Bàn Cờ Ward, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: District 3's official night food street (opened Dec 2022) on a stretch Time Out ranked among the world's coolest; ~90 stalls of bánh tráng trộn, snails and skewers, 7pm–11pm.

F.ad: Hồ Thị Kỷ, Ward 1, District 10, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A 300m alley market settled by Vietnamese-Cambodian refugees in the 1970s, now Saigon's densest Cambodian-Vietnamese food alley (100+ stalls); Khmer fish noodles, prahok and palm-sugar chè, from ~3pm.

F.n: Bún Num Bò Chóc Tư Xê
F.ad: 57/17 Hồ Thị Kỷ, Ward 1, District 10, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: The name Saigon foodies invoke for num banh chok: a golden turmeric broth built on snakehead fish and Cambodian prahok, run by Tư Xê, who brought the recipe back from Cambodia in 1972.

F.ad: 116/2/3 Phan Đăng Lưu, Ward 3, Phú Nhuận, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A 40-year alley institution off Phan Đăng Lưu famous for warm bánh đúc ladled to order with pork, wood-ear mushroom and fried shallots; once notorious for its brusque service.

F.ad: Phú Mỹ Hưng, Tân Phong Ward, District 7 / Phú Mỹ Hưng, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A home-style Korean kitchen in the heart of Phú Mỹ Hưng's Korea Town, praised for one of Saigon's most generous, fresh-made banchan spreads and its signature perilla-seed shiraegi (dried-radish-leaf) soup served with a hot stone bowl of rice. Grandma-style cooking rather than a slick BBQ chain.

F.ad: 383 Vĩnh Khánh, Ward 8, District 4, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: One of the busiest ốc (snail) houses on District 4's Vĩnh Khánh seafood strip, singled out by Rusty Compass and Will Fly for Food as a reliable, always-packed stop for cheap charcoal-grilled shellfish and stir-fried snails. English menu; open late.

F.ad: 37 Vĩnh Khánh, District 4, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A long-standing snail-and-seafood eatery near the Vĩnh Khánh corner, flagged by Rusty Compass and Will Fly for Food as one of the strip's dependable, always-busy spots. Cheap, local, sidewalk-side dining with an English-translated menu.

F.n: Hủ Tiếu Hồ Đỗ Khiêm (Đinh Hòa)
F.ad: 26 Đinh Hòa, Ward 13, District 8, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A 60-plus-year, second-generation Teochew (Triều Châu) shop on Đinh Hòa run by the Đỗ family — the reference address in Saigon for hủ tiếu hồ, a near-vanished Chaozhou dish of thin square rice sheets in a clear sweet broth served only with braised pork offal and pickled mustard greens. Busy from morning, especially weekends.

F.n: Bún Chua Cay Macao (Suan La Fen)
F.ad: 51 Bửu Đình, Ward 5, District 6, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A Hoa (Chinese-Vietnamese) family stall in a Bửu Đình alley just west of Chợ Lớn serving suan la fen — a fiery, tongue-numbing hot-and-sour noodle rooted in Chongqing, built on black vinegar and satay with dozens of toppings (spare rib, frog, beef ball, seafood) and a century-egg-in-soy starter. Order the chili level; three grades from mild to very hot.

F.ad: 200 Lê Quang Sung, Ward 2, District 6, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A 40-year Hoa dessert counter on Lê Quang Sung by Bình Tây Market, cited as District 6's most famous chè shop — heaped bowls of Chinese herbal sweet soups (chè phục linh, sâm bổ lượng) loaded with longan, lotus seed, seaweed jelly and coconut. A Chợ Lớn-west institution for chè Tàu.

F.n: Bánh Hẹ Lê Quang Sung (Khu Người Hoa)
F.ad: Lê Quang Sung, Ward 2, District 6, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A 70-year Teochew snack stall on Lê Quang Sung, in the Hoa quarter around Bình Tây / Phùng Hưng markets, that has drawn generations for bánh hẹ — pan-fried garlic-chive cakes of rice flour and hẹ — alongside taro and jicama versions. One of the last strongholds of a Chợ Lớn street snack.

F.ad: 89 Ton That Dam, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Chef Peter Cuong Franklin's retro-1960s cocktail bar above MICHELIN-starred Anan, built on Vietnam's nhau (drinking-snack) culture; Asia's 50 Best Discovery listed.

F.ad: 20 Mac Thi Buoi, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Hidden second-floor whisky-and-cocktail bar styled after a classic Tokyo whisky den, with several hundred single malts and bespoke cocktails; a Tatler Asia pick.

F.ad: 138 Nam Ky Khoi Nghia, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Subterranean Alice-in-Wonderland speakeasy (with upstairs Angels' Share) of internationally-trained bartenders, jazz nights and an Asia's-50-Best pop-up series; a Tatler Asia pick.

F.ad: 41 Nguyen Van Trang, Pham Ngu Lao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Speakeasy entered through two red London phone booths (lift the receiver to unlock the door) into a pre-war-London room of leather and mahogany; Asia's 50 Best Discovery listed.

F.ad: 63/1 Pasteur, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: New-York-style split-level speakeasy down an alleyway, all raw industrial walls and reclaimed lighting, drawing a young crowd for exemplary drinks; Asia's 50 Best Discovery listed.

F.ad: 28/3A Ton That Tung, Pham Ngu Lao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Prohibition-inspired alley speakeasy (est. 2016) with the biggest gin collection in Vietnam and 24 house gin infusions; credited with sparking Saigon's gin revival.

F.ad: 2 Lam Son Square (Park Hyatt Saigon), Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Park Hyatt Saigon's martini bar and one of the city's cocktail landmarks, running guest shifts with bartenders drawn from the World's Best Bars.

F.ad: 8A Dang Tat, Tan Dinh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Vietnam's pioneering hidden whisky bar, 600+ rare bottles curated by two collectors across intimate candlelit alcoves; named to Tatler Best Vietnam 2025.

F.ad: 39/22 Nguyen Trai, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Vietnam's first natural-wine bar (opened 2022), a tucked-away District 1 corner run by a Vietnamese sommelier with a low-intervention list.

F.ad: 63 Xuan Thuy, Thao Dien Ward, Thu Duc City, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Thao Dien wine bar from a Danish sommelier-chef couple, one of Saigon's biggest by-the-glass and bottle lists (old-world focus) with classic charcuterie.

F.ad: AB Tower, 76A Le Lai, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: The city's highest open-air rooftop bar on the 26th-27th floors of AB Tower, a 900sqm space with 360-degree skyline views, cocktails and a club sound system.

F.ad: Hotel des Arts Saigon, 76-78 Nguyen Thi Minh Khai, Vo Thi Sau Ward, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Rooftop bar and infinity pool on the 23rd-24th floors of the elegant Hotel des Arts, a stylish sunset-to-late spot over the District 3 skyline.

F.ad: Caravelle Saigon, 19-23 Lam Son Square, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Historic 10th-floor rooftop bar atop the Caravelle Hotel, a wartime haunt of diplomats and correspondents since 1959, with live music and skyline views.

F.ad: 144/3 Pasteur, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: The alley taproom where Saigon's craft-beer story began in 2015; 70+ recipes built on Vietnamese ingredients (jasmine, passionfruit, cacao), pioneers of the scene.

F.ad: 31D Ly Tu Trong, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Conrad-themed brewery-taproom (est. 2016) with 20 rotating taps of bold, hop-forward beers; one of Saigon's most awarded craft breweries.

F.ad: 181-185 Ly Tu Trong, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Saigon's first in-house brewpub concept, a large downtown brewery-and-kitchen turning out an approachable core range with local twists.

F.ad: 1 Le Ngo Cat, Ward 7, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Collaborative craft-beer house pouring nearly 50 Vietnamese beers on tap alongside gastropub food; a hub of the local brewing community.

F.ad: 50 Dang Thi Nhu, Nguyen Thai Binh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Art-Deco-Indochine taproom near Bui Vien over three levels to a rooftop terrace, brewing approachable styles with Southeast Asian ingredients and local collaborations.

F.ad: 40 Bui Vien, Pham Ngu Lao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Casual Bui Vien taproom of an entirely-Vietnamese brand (est. 2015) built for easy drinking rather than transplanted US craft culture.

F.ad: 90 Nguyen Van Thu, Da Kao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Da Kao taproom of one of Saigon's early homegrown breweries (est. 2015), pairing eight house beers with a relaxed Vietnamese-tapas dining room.

F.ad: 220A Nguyen Cong Tru, Nguyen Thai Binh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A colonial-shophouse coffee experience space and roastery telling Vietnam's 160-year coffee story; signature phin, filter and espresso blends plus cold brew and cascara.

F.ad: 103bis Vo Thi Sau, Ward 6, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Specialty coffeehouse and in-house roastery (est. 2018) in a restored 1950s house, with a garden-linked Blue in Green roasting room you can watch at work.

F.ad: 40/8 Pham Viet Chanh, Ward 19, Binh Thanh District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Cafe of Building, the Will Frith co-roasting hub and consultancy behind much of Saigon's specialty scene; precise brews from a serious roasting operation.

F.ad: Thảo Điền, Thủ Đức City, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Chef Cường Nguyễn (ex-sous chef of MICHELIN-starred Anan Saigon) reinvents Vietnamese comfort food in a stately Thảo Điền villa; a MICHELIN Selected restaurant (2023 inaugural list, in the 2026 Guide) with a coveted eight-seat Chef's Table.

F.ad: Nguyễn Văn Linh, Tân Phong Ward, District 7 (Phú Mỹ Hưng), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A decade-old Korean cold-noodle specialist run by owner Joo Won-mi in D7's Koreatown, its back looking onto the Phú Mỹ Hưng enclave; Saigoneer calls it the city's best naengmyeon.

F.ad: 38 Nguyễn Ư Dĩ, Thảo Điền, Thủ Đức City, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Saigon's benchmark riverside restaurant-bar (since 2008) on a near-rural stretch of the Saigon River; named by The Guardian among the world's best bars, and Rusty Compass's pick for the city's best riverside meal.

F.ad: Thảo Điền, Thủ Đức City, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Thảo Điền wine bar helmed by Osaka-born sommelier Yu Yamamoto, the first winner of the MICHELIN Guide Vietnam Sommelier Award (2023); farm-sourced European-Japanese plates against an outstanding wine list.

F.ad: 19 Đường Số 2, Thảo Điền, Thủ Đức City, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: The Thảo Điền outpost of XLIII (formerly 43 Factory Coffee Roaster), a transparency-first specialty roaster since 2018, set in a courtyard house of traditional Vietnamese architecture; ultra-light roasts and precise pour-overs.

F.ad: Ngô Quang Huy, Thảo Điền, Thủ Đức City, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Chef-owner Thierry Mounon's elegant colonial villa off Thảo Điền serving classic French gastronomy from the southwest; a MICHELIN Selected restaurant (2023 & 2024) with a deep French wine list.

F.ad: Thảo Điền, Thủ Đức City, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: An intimate ~18-seat Thảo Điền izakaya that layers Japanese pub culture with occidental luxe ingredients at friendly prices; a contemporary take praised by Vietcetera and Saigoneer.

F.ad: 6/1/2 Nguyễn Ư Dĩ, Thảo Điền, Thủ Đức City, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Danish couple Camilla Bailey and Casper Gustafsen's converted villa ('mad' means food in Danish) under shady tropical trees; clean Scandinavian flavours, weekend acoustic sets and an award for the city's best neighbourhood hangout.

F.ad: Thảo Điền, Thủ Đức City, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Thảo Điền's oldest surviving expat cafe (since 2004), a rustic hidden-courtyard mainstay from the owners of The Deck; Mediterranean cooking with Asian flavours, breakfast through late evening.

F.ad: District 7 (Phú Mỹ Hưng), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A homey D7 Koreatown kitchen focused on wholesome, health-minded cooking with one of Saigon's most generous, frequently-changing banchan spreads; a Saigoneer Hẻm Gems feature.

F.ad: District 7 (Phú Mỹ Hưng), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A small D7 Thai-noodle spot run by Quan, who cooked in Thai restaurants during a decade in Australia; punchy, takeout-friendly bowls spotlighted by Saigoneer's Hẻm Gems.

F.ad: Thảo Điền, Thủ Đức City, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: The Thảo Điền branch of one of Saigon's most-loved French patisseries, in a three-floor glass building (bakery-cafe below, bistro above); minimalist design, organic local fruit and biodegradable cassava-starch packaging.

F.ad: Đường Nguyễn Văn Công, Ward 3, Gò Vấp, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: The original plane-spotting café: from the 2nd- and 3rd-floor balconies you look straight down the Tân Sơn Nhất runway as jets roar in to land every few minutes, sunset being the golden hour. Drinks and light bites 30–70k VND. Featured by VnExpress and Dân Trí as one of Saigon's two runway-view cafés.

F.ad: Đường Nguyễn Văn Công, Ward 3, Gò Vấp, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: The milk-tea-leaning sibling right next door to Phen's, with its own open-air balcony over the same Tân Sơn Nhất runway — coffee, tea, yoghurt and smoothies 28–46k VND while planes drop overhead. Named alongside Phen's in the VnExpress / Dân Trí runway-café features.

F.ad: 672A50 Phan Văn Trị, Ward 10, Gò Vấp, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A 24/7 multi-level check-in café whose façade and interior are covered in more than 700 teddy bears — from palm-sized plush to a 2.5 m giant — a ~500 million VND build by owner Trần Thế Hiển that went viral (and mildly controversial) across TikTok in 2025. A Gò Vấp 'sống ảo' phenomenon, not a specialty-coffee destination.

F.ad: Alley off Quang Trung (An Hội / An Nhơn ward), Gò Vấp, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Saigon's only Nigerian kitchen, tucked in a Gò Vấp courtyard behind a red 'Baby African Restaurant' sign and running informally out of the owner's home for nearly 20 years — jollof rice, African fried rice, egusi soup and stews. A repeat Saigoneer Hẻm Gems subject ('The Legend of Baby African' and 'Reliving the Joy of Jollof Rice').

F.n: Hủ Tiếu Mì Gốc Hoa Ông Há (Phan Huy Ích)
F.ad: Đường Phan Huy Ích, Ward 12, Gò Vấp, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A family Hoa (ethnic-Chinese) egg-noodle shop on Phan Huy Ích that has held its recipe for ~38 years in Saigon's outer edge — springy hủ tiếu mì with hoành thánh (wontons). Documented by VnExpress both in a dedicated profile and in its citywide hủ tiếu round-up.

F.ad: Cô Giang Street, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: An 80-year-old cháo lòng (pork-offal congee) gánh that started at Cầu Muối market and still cooks its silky congee in a hand-welded pot made from two aluminium basins turned mouth-to-mouth. Three generations in; Bà Út alone has ladled it for over 60 years, and the menu has never changed.

F.ad: Hai Bà Trưng Street (near hẻm 191), District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A more-than-70-year-old northern-style bánh mì tray (mẹt) sold from the pavement, its loaves stacked on a woven tray the way Cụ Lý carried them from the North in the 1950s. Named a Top 10 long-running (50+ year) bánh mì brand by the Vietnam Record Organization in 2023; sells hundreds of loaves each morning.

F.ad: 19 Nguyễn Huy Tự, Đa Kao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: An ice-cream shop open since 1958, whose founder Cụ Lý Thân learned the craft in Cambodia before setting up in Đa Kao; now run by the third/fourth generation on a near-70-year recipe. Its tube ice cream (kem ống) and kem ký are churned from condensed milk, coconut, beans, sweet potato and fresh fruit — a genuine 1950s Saigon taste that has found a new gen-Z following.

F.n: Bánh Canh Cua 194 Võ Văn Tần
F.ad: 194 Võ Văn Tần (đầu hẻm), District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A bánh canh cua (crab tapioca-noodle soup) counter at the mouth of alley 194 that Võ Kim Hồng's grandmother started in the early 1980s — over 40 years and now into the fourth generation. Its signature is bánh canh cua xào, stir-fried freshly-molted crab from a long-time Bến Thành supplier.

F.ad: 50 Hồ Biểu Chánh, Ward 12, Phú Nhuận District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A three-generation Hanoi-style bún thang house, its clear-sweet broth simmered from chicken bones and dried shrimp and topped with the dish's fine julienne of egg, chicken and giò. A long-loved pocket of northern refinement in Phú Nhuận, now run by third-generation owner Bích Ngọc.

F.ad: Lô I chung cư Ngô Gia Tự, Ward 2, District 10, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A pork-offal congee stall opened in 1977 under the Ngô Gia Tự apartments, its garlic-fragrant, smooth cháo and sweet giò chìa unchanged across 45+ years and two generations. Nicknamed 'cháo bụi' by comedian Việt Hương, a regular from before she was famous.

F.ad: Chợ Lớn, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A Chinese-Vietnamese bánh mì brand in Chợ Lớn established in 1968, distinguished by its roasted pâté and a strongly Cantonese-flavoured xíu mại (siu mai) that sets it apart from central or northern versions. Named a Top 10 long-running (50+ year) bánh mì brand by the Vietnam Record Organization.

F.ad: 11A Cao Thắng, Ward 2, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A northern-style bánh cuốn shop of more than half a century on a two-metre-wide Cao Thắng storefront, where — however crowded — the cook still hand-pours each rice-and-tapioca crêpe to order rather than using a machine. A quiet multi-generation Saigon fixture.

F.ad: Thuận Kiều Street, Ward 4, District 11, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: The oldest cơm tấm (broken-rice) brand in Saigon, born on Thuận Kiều Street in Chợ Lớn before 1975 and named for it. A pioneer that broadened cơm tấm beyond the classic sườn-bì-chả with dishes like grilled chicken and cá lóc kho, it has anchored District 11 for generations.

F.n: Bún Bò Dồi Chiên Cô Minh
F.ad: Phan Xích Long, Phú Nhuận District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A bún bò counter open since 1984 whose one-of-a-kind twist is dồi chiên — fried blood-and-herb sausage — dropped into the bowl, a recipe unchanged for nearly four decades and passed down from the owner's elder sister. Around 300 bowls a day; the stall has moved several times but only grown.

F.ad: 166 Phó Cơ Điều (chợ Thiếc), Ward 6, District 11, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A pavement súp cua (crab soup) stall by chợ Thiếc that has drawn packed evening crowds for over 20 years, ladling out around 10 pots a day thick with crab, quail egg, pig brain and marrow. A cheap, beloved chợ-Thiếc institution profiled repeatedly in the local press.

F.n: Bún Riêu Cua Ốc Thanh Hải
F.ad: 14/12 Kỳ Đồng, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A northern-style bún ốc riêu cua tucked in an alley off Kỳ Đồng since 1982, cooked by Thái Bình-born Phạm Thị Hải, who keeps the field-crab-and-snail broth exactly as her family ate it back home. Over 40 years of a homesick Bắc flavour rarely found in the South.

F.n: Gỏi Khô Bò Công Viên Lê Văn Tám
F.ad: Hai Bà Trưng Street (opposite Lê Văn Tám Park), District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A near-50-year gỏi khô bò (green-papaya salad with dried beef) stall on the pavement facing Lê Văn Tám Park — a sub-1-metre table and a glass case that has become a Saigon street-food legend. Crisp shredded papaya, chewy dried beef and a sweet-sour-spicy sauce; foreign visitors now queue and eat sitting on the kerb.

F.ad: 9 Huỳnh Khương Ninh, Đa Kao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A more-than-60-year bánh mì shop named for its founder — the seventh child, Quang — famous for a pâté that regulars swear by and a flavour they say has never changed. It began at the Đinh Tiên Hoàng corner before settling on Huỳnh Khương Ninh.

F.ad: 43 Tôn Thất Đạm, Nguyễn Thái Bình Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A 60–70-year hủ tiếu cá landmark on Tôn Thất Đạm, its wide, soft rice noodles and clear Cantonese-sweet broth crowned with wafer-thin slices of fish — a Hoa-Việt fusion that is a point of Saigon pride. So loved that singer Hari Won has been photographed waiting before it opens.

F.ad: 318/1 Bùi Hữu Nghĩa, Ward 1, Bình Thạnh District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A famed evening xôi gà (chicken sticky-rice) gánh hidden behind a power pole near chợ Bà Chiểu, selling hundreds of packets a night despite having no seats. Chicken, Chinese sausage and offal versions, ladled by a stall that has become a Bình Thạnh ritual.

F.ad: Corner of Trương Định & Nguyễn An Ninh, Bến Thành Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A single-dish bún mọc house beside Bến Thành market, going since 1980 from a small gánh to a corner shop, its steaming bowl piled with sườn, mọc and four kinds of chả. The pork balls are hand-made from giò sống and wood-ear, the broth skimmed clear — over 40 years of northern flavour in the centre of town.

F.ad: 12 Nguyễn Huy Tự, Đa Kao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A cháo lòng stall opposite Đa Kao market that Đa Kao locals have known since the 1960s — over 50 years and three generations. Its signature dồi is stuffed not with the usual blood and herbs but with marinated, fried pork tenderloin, which is why it sits among the priciest bowls in town.

F.n: Mì Vịt Tiềm Quảng Huê Viên
F.ad: Corner of Phan Đình Phùng & Nguyễn Trọng Tuyển, Phú Nhuận District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: One of Saigon's oldest Cantonese kitchens, traced by its owners to a 1940 congee shop and famous for 70+ years across three generations for mì vịt tiềm — herbal-stewed duck, its skin both chewy and crisp, over springy egg noodles. Small and not cheap, but a Hoa culinary heirloom.

F.ad: Hẻm 241 Bến Vân Đồn, Ward 2, District 4, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A dawn cơm tấm hidden in an alley off Bến Vân Đồn, open from 4am and sold out by 9am, run for over 40 years by Cô Phượng and her daughters on the mother's marinades for sườn and pâté. A District 4 breakfast institution eaten in front of an old house.

F.ad: 14 Nguyen Truong To, Ward 2, Vung Tau, Vietnam
F.w: The most famous banh khot house in Vung Tau, the city that owns the dish: tiny turmeric-coconut rice pancakes crowned with fresh shrimp, wood-fired by a line of women and wrapped in mustard leaf with herbs and nuoc cham. One of the oldest, and always a queue. ~07:00-14:00.

F.ad: Phu My Hung (Sky Garden / Hung Gia), District 7, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Saigon's Koreatown: the Sky Garden / Hung Gia blocks of Phu My Hung, home to ~20,000 Korean residents and a dense run of authentic Korean BBQ joints, soft-tofu-stew and cold-noodle houses, K-cafes and K-beauty shops - the real thing, run for the community.

F.ad: Xom Luoi, Ward 2, Vung Tau, Vietnam
F.w: The locals' seafood market where the day's catch lands each afternoon (~15:00-16:00): pick prawns, crab, snails and fish from the tanks and have a stall grill or steam them on the spot for a small fee - Vung Tau's cheapest, freshest seafood feed.

F.ad: Dai Tam, My Xuyen, Can Tho, Vietnam
F.w: A ~100-year-old Mekong specialty: a deep-fried mung-bean, pork and whole-shrimp fritter eaten with herbs and sweet-sour sauce, at its source in the old Khmer village of Dai Tam (formerly Soc Trang). A cluster of ~15 family stalls near Dai Tam market, from mid-morning.

F.ad: 9F, Le Méridien Saigon, 3C Ton Duc Thang, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: One MICHELIN Star (2024-2026); chef Sam Aisbett's modern Australian tasting menu with Japanese technique and Vietnamese produce, high above the river at Le Méridien.

F.ad: 4F, The Reverie Saigon, 22-36 Nguyen Hue, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: One MICHELIN Star; chef Angus Chan's refined Cantonese kitchen inside The Reverie, weaving Vietnamese ingredients into Hong Kong technique amid jade and gold-leaf interiors.

F.ad: 50 6/3 Street, Thao Dien Ward, Thu Duc City, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: One MICHELIN Star (2025 debut); an intimate Thao Dien villa where French technique fuses with Vietnamese soul across an ever-evolving tasting menu.

F.ad: 143 Nam Ky Khoi Nghia, Vo Thi Sau Ward, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Promoted to One MICHELIN Star in 2025; chef Thanh Vuong Vo's contemporary Vietnamese cooking with fermentation and modern flair, plus a whisky bar.

F.ad: 93-97 Dong Khoi, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: MICHELIN Selected; celebrity chef Luke Nguyen elevates traditional Vietnamese cooking in a colonial Dong Khoi townhouse — duck noodle soup, char-grilled chicken, silken tofu dessert.

F.ad: 74/7 Hai Ba Trung, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: MICHELIN Selected two years running; a polished take on Saigon classics set in a restored 1900s opium refinery with an al fresco Parisian-style courtyard.

F.ad: 37bis Ky Con, Nguyen Thai Binh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: MICHELIN Selected; produce-driven Mediterranean cooking from two wood-fired ovens in a renovated heritage house, led by chef Julien Perraudin.

F.ad: 23F, Hôtel des Arts Saigon, 76-78 Nguyen Thi Minh Khai, Vo Thi Sau Ward, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: MICHELIN Selected; two-Michelin-star chef Kirk Westaway reimagines British classics — fish and chips, roast chicken with thyme, Eton mess — 23 floors above the city.

F.ad: 6F, 12 Phan Ke Binh, Da Kao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: MICHELIN Selected (2025); central-Vietnamese cooking in a wooden house of lotus ponds and lanterns that recreates the feel of old Hoi An town.

F.ad: 2F, Sofitel Saigon Plaza, 17 Le Duan, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: MICHELIN Selected; contemporary Vietnamese menu built around prize-winning ST25 rice, run by social enterprise KOTO inside the Sofitel.

F.ad: 10 Tran Ngoc Dien, Thao Dien Ward, Thu Duc City, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: MICHELIN Selected; modern central-Vietnamese cooking from the chef's home region, served in an Indochine Art Deco room in Thao Dien.

F.ad: 125/12 Nguyen Cuu Van, Ward 17, Binh Thanh District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: MICHELIN Selected and Sommelier Award 2025; fine-dining fusion with a strong wine program tucked down an alley in Binh Thanh.

F.ad: 53 Tran Nhat Duat, Tan Dinh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: MICHELIN Selected (2026); a tasting menu that journeys from northern to central to southern Vietnam, each floor themed to a region — elegant Hue beef noodle, fish soup with caviar.

F.ad: 215B37 Nguyen Van Huong, An Khanh Ward, Thu Duc City, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: MICHELIN Selected (2026); chef Kien Phan's grill-focused, à la carte Vietnamese cooking blending tradition and modernity in a serene Thao Dien alley.

F.ad: 23C Le Van Mien, An Khanh Ward, Thu Duc City, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: MICHELIN Selected (2025); a garden-terrace kitchen where the chef melds Western technique with local soul, backed by shelves of house-made ferments.

F.ad: 10 Nguyen Thanh Y, Da Kao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: MICHELIN Selected (2026); Vietnam's first zero-waste plant-based fine dining, a seasonal menu sourced from a Da Lat eco-farm and the restaurant's rooftop garden.

F.ad: 32 Street D10, Thao Dien Ward, Thu Duc City, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: MICHELIN Selected; Vietnamese-inspired vegetarian cooking with modern twists using organic farm produce, set around a leafy courtyard and patio.

F.ad: 26B Street 10, Thao Dien Ward, Thu Duc City, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: MICHELIN Selected; the city's only Michelin-listed vegetarian house, a two-level rustic-chic room serving Vietnamese dishes alongside Western and Thai plates.

F.ad: 2 Le Van Mien, Thao Dien Ward, Thu Duc City, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: MICHELIN Selected (2025); a neighbourhood food bar in Thao Dien serving inventive small plates that cross cuisines.

F.ad: 45 Nguyen Duy Hieu, Thao Dien Ward, Thu Duc City, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: MICHELIN Selected (2026); an unpretentious open-kitchen Italian in Thao Dien with pasta the highlight — rich carbonara with crispy bacon and parmesan.

F.ad: 21 Han Thuyen, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: MICHELIN Selected; a bright, retro-era bistro opposite the cathedral serving contemporary Vietnamese street food with homemade tofu and bread.

F.ad: 82 Cu Xa Nguyen Van Troi, Ward 17, Phu Nhuan District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: MICHELIN Selected (2026); a decades-old family kitchen tucked in the old Nguyen Van Troi apartment quarters, serving Hue central-Vietnamese home cooking to generations of regulars.

F.ad: 40A Tran Cao Van, Ward 6, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: MICHELIN Selected; a snail-and-seafood specialist down a narrow District 3 alley — snails in coconut soup, curry, or steamed with fresh peppercorn.

F.ad: 84/6 Nguyen Bieu, Ward 1, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: MICHELIN Bib Gourmand; a tiny, decades-old shop whose thick-noodle crab banh canh in a rich tomato-crab broth draws queues (closed Wednesdays).

F.ad: 1346 Truong Sa, Tan Son Hoa Ward, Phu Nhuan District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: MICHELIN Bib Gourmand (2026); a bustling canalside corner where the bún riêu comes in a tomato-and-crab broth topped with fresh whelk and minced pork.

F.ad: 32 Street D11, Thao Dien Ward, Thu Duc City, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: MICHELIN Bib Gourmand (2024); a long-running Thao Dien favourite with a nature-themed interior and a broad menu of regional Vietnamese specialties, claypots and hotpots.

F.ad: 112 Ly Tu Trong, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: MICHELIN Bib Gourmand (2024); Malaysian chef Adrian Chong Yen's pan-Latin-American plates — Mexican empanadas, Peruvian scallop ceviche — in the city centre.

F.ad: Hẻm off Lê Quang Định, Bình Thạnh, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: The matriarchs of Bình Thạnh's 'Chicken Corner' have grilled charcoal gà nướng since 1996 — smoky, juicy whole chicken, one dish done perfectly, eaten on plastic stools deep in a hẻm near the Gò Vấp border. A Saigoneer Hẻm Gems pick that Vietnam Coracle also singles out.

F.ad: Văn Thánh Market, Ward 25, Bình Thạnh, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A sprawling local wet market in the shadow of Pearl Plaza with dozens of cheap, no-frills street-food vendors — morning bún thịt nướng grilled streetside and the Hải Phòng specialty bánh đa cua are the standouts. The subject of a dedicated Vietnam Coracle food deep-dive.

F.ad: Phan Văn Hân Street, Bình Thạnh, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A student-packed open-air food street on the District 1 / Bình Thạnh edge where single-dish stalls have specialized for 20+ years — bột chiên, bánh tráng trộn, gỏi cuốn, mì vịt tiềm and a beloved 40k-VND bún bò Huế. Mapped stop-by-stop in a Vietcetera foodie guide.

F.ad: 08 Nguyễn Giao, KP2, Quốc lộ 22, Củ Chi, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: The landmark bò tơ Củ Chi house — young free-range beef (calves only 5–6 months) served as a hotpot and grilled, wrapped in rice paper with dew-soaked bánh tráng and mountains of herbs. A 30-year Highway 22 institution reviewed by Việt Nam News as a southern classic worth the drive.

F.n: Bánh Canh Trảng Bàng Út Huệ
F.ad: 88 Nguyễn Văn Rốp, Trảng Bàng, Tây Ninh, Vietnam
F.w: The Bùi-family bánh canh that defines Tây Ninh's most famous food stop — clear pork-bone broth, hand-cut chewy rice noodles and crisp boiled pork leg, eaten with a plate of fresh herbs. One of the two landmark bánh canh Trảng Bàng houses on Nguyễn Văn Rốp.

F.n: Bánh Canh Trảng Bàng Năm Dung
F.ad: 90 Nguyễn Văn Rốp, Trảng Bàng, Tây Ninh, Vietnam
F.w: A bánh canh name Trảng Bàng locals have known since the 1950s, right beside Út Huệ — the same dew-soaked-rice-paper canon of clear broth, pork leg and hand-made noodles. The old-guard alternative for the town's signature bowl.

F.n: Bánh Tráng Phơi Sương Trảng Bàng
F.ad: Trảng Bàng town, Tây Ninh, Vietnam
F.w: The town's other signature: dew-soaked rice paper, sun-dried by day then softened in the night dew, whose craft was named national intangible cultural heritage in 2016. Eaten as bánh tráng cuốn thịt luộc — soft-paper rolls of boiled pork belly, herbs and dipping salt. Buy fresh from Trảng Bàng makers or eat it rolled at any bánh canh house here.

F.n: Cơm Chay Long Hoa (Tây Ninh Vegetarian)
F.ad: Long Hoa Market area, Hòa Thành, Tây Ninh, Vietnam
F.w: The densest vegetarian-food zone in Vietnam, feeding the Cao Đài faithful who fast at least 10 days a month — mì Quảng chay, bún riêu chay, vegetarian spring rolls and mock-meat skewers made from Tây Ninh soy and sesame. The Long Hoa cluster by the Holy See is the place to taste this deeply local chay tradition.

F.n: Bánh Tráng Muối Tôm Tây Ninh
F.ad: Long Hoa Market, Hòa Thành, Tây Ninh, Vietnam
F.w: Tây Ninh's viral street snack and famous souvenir: rice-paper strips tossed with the province's signature muối tôm (shrimp-chili salt), dried shrimp, quail eggs, mango and herbs. The muối tôm — salt roasted with dried shrimp, garlic and chili — is the reason people bring bags of it home.

F.ad: Trung An & Củ Chi town, Củ Chi, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Củ Chi's beloved cassava — sweeter, chewier and more fragrant than elsewhere — steamed with pineapple leaf and eaten with sesame or chili salt, the same tuber that fed the tunnel fighters. A cheap, nostalgic roadside snack sold across the district.

F.ad: Núi Bà Đen foothills, Tây Ninh, Vietnam
F.w: Mountain snails found only around Bà Đen, foraged after rain and cooked stuffed with grated coconut, steamed with lemongrass or ginger and dipped in salt-pepper-lime. A genuinely place-specific Tây Ninh delicacy eaten at the foot of the mountain.

F.ad: 59C Thuận Kiều, Ward 12, District 5 (Cholon), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Cholon's beloved Cantonese duck-noodle house — cinnamon-scented broth, lightly seasoned juicy braised duck, house-made egg noodles. A Saigoneer Hẻm Gems feature.

F.n: Hủ Tiếu Sa Tế Quảng Ký
F.ad: 117 Triệu Quang Phục, Ward 11, District 5 (Cholon), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Teochew satay-noodle specialist in Cholon — a spicy-savoury broth built from 30+ condiments, a signature Chợ Lớn dish brought by 19th-century Teochew migrants.

F.ad: District 5 (Cholon), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A 30-year Cholon institution that grew from a single chè stall into a symbol of Chinese-Vietnamese sweets — egg-in-tea chè and almond chè among the classics.

F.ad: 534 Vĩnh Khánh, District 4, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: The most famous ốc house on District 4's Vĩnh Khánh seafood strip (~20 years); a MICHELIN Bib Gourmand 2024 pick, signature salt-roasted crab claws, plastic-stool buzz.

F.ad: Vĩnh Khánh, District 4, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A long-loved Saigon ốc name known for fresh, well-seasoned snails and grilled shellfish; a fixture of the District 4 Vĩnh Khánh seafood-street scene.

F.ad: Bình Thạnh District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: One of Bình Thạnh's best-known bún bò Huế houses, styled like a countryside home — a beloved local institution in one of Saigon's most underrated street-food districts.

F.ad: 35 Xuân Thủy, Thảo Điền, District 2 (Thủ Đức City), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A reinvented modern-Vietnamese space in Thảo Điền; a MICHELIN Selected restaurant (2023) spotlighted in Saigon's 'new Vietnamese' wave.

F.ad: 22 Đặng Hữu Phổ, Thảo Điền, District 2 (Thủ Đức City), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A tranquil green villa in Thảo Điền serving authentic Vietnamese with a gentle modern twist and vegetarian focus — a District 2 expat favourite.

F.ad: Thảo Điền, District 2 (Thủ Đức City), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A health-leaning all-day brunch villa in a spacious Thảo Điền garden — a mainstay of District 2's expat brunch scene.

F.ad: Thảo Điền, District 2, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam (also Lê Lợi & Đồng Khởi, District 1)
F.w: A pioneering concept-store cafe-bistro brand that keeps innovating brunch with Vietnamese ingredients; the Thảo Điền outlet anchors District 2.

F.ad: 6E Tú Xương, Võ Thị Sáu Ward, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam (flagship roastery in Thảo Điền, District 2)
F.w: Called 'the specialty coffee of the moment' — a sustainability-minded Vietnamese roaster championing single origins from Buôn Ma Thuột and beyond.

F.ad: 27 Lưu Văn Lang, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Widely regarded as one of the city's best practitioners of specialty coffee — serious brew hardware, Vietnamese and international beans, standout egg coffee.

F.ad: 193 Hai Bà Trưng, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A true farm-to-cup Vietnamese roaster growing its beans in Dalat's Central Highlands — one of the country's defining specialty brands.

F.ad: 26 Lý Tự Trọng & Nguyễn Huệ, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam (multiple branches)
F.w: The retro, olive-green subsidy-era chain that made cà phê cốt dừa (coconut coffee) a Saigon signature — a near-obligatory coconut-coffee stop.

F.ad: 22 Lê Lợi, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam (branches incl. Thảo Điền, District 2)
F.w: A sleek retro-Saigon small-batch roaster near Bến Thành that blends traditional Vietnamese coffee with modern specialty craft across its city outlets.

F.ad: Saigon Pearl, Nguyễn Hữu Cảnh, Bình Thạnh District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A multi-storey riverside coffee mansion (opened 2016) that helped awaken Vietnam's Arabica specialty scene and trained national barista champions.

F.ad: 1st floor, 136 Lê Thánh Tôn, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Saigon's highest-placed bar on Asia's 50 Best Bars (ranked 2022-2025, No. 61 in 2025) — a speakeasy-jazz room of precise modern-classic drinks.

F.ad: 2nd floor, 63 Đồng Du, Bến Nghé Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: An artful cocktail bar in an old colonial apartment — bar director Jay Moir's spirited, botanical-and-spice list; featured on World's 50 Best Discovery.

F.ad: District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Layla's experimental sibling and a sustainability-driven cocktail lab — Saigon's sole entrant on Asia's 50 Best Bars 51-100 in 2021 (No. 77).

F.ad: Tôn Đức Thắng, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A renovated century-old colonial mansion pairing local Vietnamese ingredients with modern technique — Asia's 50 Best Bars No. 93 (2025) and Tatler's Vietnam Bar of the Year 2025.

F.ad: 1st floor, 14 Tôn Thất Đạm, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A 1920s New York-styled speakeasy specialising in classic cocktails and mixology — one of the bars that seeded Saigon's speakeasy wave.

F.ad: Kỳ Đồng, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A 40-year Saigon chè institution on Kỳ Đồng street — a wide spread of sweet soups and the authentic ambience of a street-side dessert shop.

F.n: Bánh Bông Lan Trứng Muối Gốc Cột Điện
F.ad: Nguyễn Thái Học, Phường 7, Vũng Tàu, Bà Rịa–Vũng Tàu, Vietnam
F.w: Vũng Tàu's originator of bánh bông lan trứng muối (salted-egg sponge cake), open since 1986 — a feather-light sponge loaded with salted egg yolk, cheese and pork floss. Named for the electric pole (cột điện) it started beside; the cake that made this a citywide take-home specialty.

F.ad: 44 Trương Công Định, Phường 3, Vũng Tàu, Bà Rịa–Vũng Tàu, Vietnam
F.w: The best-known address for lẩu cá đuối (stingray hotpot) — Vũng Tàu's signature dish: sweet, chewy stingray in a sour-spicy tamarind-and-pickled-bamboo broth. A long-running budget seafood institution on Trương Công Định.

F.ad: 3 Trần Phú, Front Beach (Bãi Trước), Phường 5, Vũng Tàu, Bà Rịa–Vũng Tàu, Vietnam
F.w: Vũng Tàu's legendary open-air seafood house, sprawling over a rocky waterfront where waves break metres from the table — fresh crab, prawns and grilled fish with a sunset sea view. The classic Front Beach seafood stop for weekending Saigonese.

F.ad: 11 Cách Mạng Tháng Tám, Long Hương, Bà Rịa, Bà Rịa–Vũng Tàu, Vietnam
F.w: The famous 'cổng chào' (welcome-gate) bánh canh at the entrance to Bà Rịa — thick chewy rice-tapioca noodles in a marrow-rich pork broth, topped with the signature xương que nạc (meaty pork rib). A mandatory pit-stop on the drive to Vũng Tàu.

F.ad: Quốc lộ 55, An Nhứt, Long Điền, Bà Rịa–Vũng Tàu, Vietnam
F.w: A 60-year-old roadside institution in An Nhứt village (Long Điền) making bánh hỏi — gossamer, net-woven rice-vermicelli sheets from local Long Điền rice, served with grilled meat, chives oil and herbs. The area's defining specialty on the QL55 corridor.

F.ad: Quốc lộ 51, Long Thành, Đồng Nai, Vietnam
F.w: The roadside dairy that everyone stops for en route to Vũng Tàu — Long Thành's fresh pasteurised cow's milk and its take-home bánh sữa (milk cakes) and kẹo sữa (milk candy), a recognised Đồng Nai regional specialty since the 1980s.

F.ad: Nam Kỳ Khởi Nghĩa, Phường 1, TP. Mỹ Tho, Tiền Giang, Vietnam
F.w: One of five eateries certified 'Quán hủ tiếu Mỹ Tho uy tín, chất lượng 2024' by Tiền Giang province — the definitive stop for hủ tiếu Mỹ Tho, the dry or soup rice-noodle dish built on chewy Gò Cát noodles, clear pork-and-dried-squid broth and a scatter of toppings. A long-running, no-frills local institution.

F.ad: TP. Mỹ Tho, Tiền Giang, Vietnam
F.w: Another of the five province-certified Mỹ Tho hủ tiếu houses (2024), this one specialising in the fish version — hủ tiếu cá — with sweet snakehead fish over the same trademark Mỹ Tho rice noodles. A local favourite that shows the dish beyond its standard pork form.

F.ad: 188 Trần Hưng Đạo, Phường 1, TP. Sa Đéc, Đồng Tháp, Vietnam
F.w: A 50-year-old Sa Đéc noodle counter (open since 1968) famous for a MSG-free, bone-simmered Chinese-style broth and the silky rice noodles made from Sa Đéc's century-old flour village. Bowls have long started at almost nothing; go at lunch to beat the morning and evening crush.

F.ad: TP. Bến Tre, Bến Tre, Vietnam
F.w: The signature edible souvenir of the 'coconut land'. Thanh Long, founded 1970 by Nguyễn Thị Vinh — whose portrait on the wrapper became a symbol of Bến Tre — is one of the province's landmark coconut-candy brands, cooking and cutting the chewy caramel by hand and exporting to the US and Australia. Try it warm off the tray at a working workshop.

F.ad: 86/38 Lý Tự Trọng, Ninh Kiều, Cần Thơ, Vietnam
F.w: The best-known address for bánh cống, Cần Thơ's Khmer-origin fritter — a deep tube-mould of rice batter, mung bean and a whole shrimp fried golden and crisp, eaten with herbs and sweet-sour fish sauce. A cheap, beloved late-afternoon Tây Đô snack down a small alley off Lý Tự Trọng.

F.ad: 17 Đại Lộ Hòa Bình, P. Tân An, Ninh Kiều, Cần Thơ, Vietnam
F.w: Cần Thơ's most famous house for nem nướng Cái Răng — grilled pork balls seared over charcoal and rolled at the table with bánh hỏi, herbs, green banana, starfruit and pickled lemongrass in soft rice paper, dipped in a sweet-savoury sauce. A city institution on Hòa Bình boulevard.

F.n: Bánh Tét Lá Cẩm Nhà Họ Huỳnh
F.ad: Bùi Hữu Nghĩa, P. Bình Thủy, Cần Thơ, Vietnam
F.w: The Bình Thủy family lò that invented Cần Thơ's purple bánh tét — matriarch Huỳnh Thị Trọng (bà Sáu Trọng) first soaked the sticky rice in lá cẩm (magenta-plant) juice, wrapping it around mung bean, pork fat and salted egg. Now made by three-plus generations, it was named among Vietnam's Top 100 dishes/specialties (2017).

F.n: Penang Road Famous Jin Kor Char Kuey Teow
F.ad: Lebuh Keng Kwee (off Jalan Penang), George Town, Penang, Malaysia
F.w: ~40-year charcoal stall in the Penang Road cendol lane; MICHELIN Guide-listed for its cockle-and-prawn char koay teow with pronounced wok hei.

F.ad: 177 Jalan Penang (alley at Lebuh Chulia junction), George Town, Penang, Malaysia
F.w: Penang's most legendary 24-hour nasi kandar, cooked in a narrow lane since the 1940s; the 'flooded' curry-mix rice and fried chicken are institutions.

F.ad: Beside Air Itam Market, Jalan Pasar, Air Itam, Penang, Malaysia
F.w: The definitive Air Itam asam laksa; CNN Travel ranked Penang asam laksa among the World's 50 Best Foods. Reopened after a pandemic pause; now weekends only.

F.ad: Jalan Yau Tet Shin, Ipoh, Perak, Malaysia (relocating to a larger nearby space in 2026)
F.w: Ipoh's iconic tauge ayam since 1957 — poached chicken, blanched bean sprouts and smooth hor fun. Anthony Bourdain ate here; still open, moving to a bigger site in 2026.

F.ad: 5 Jalan SS21/37, Damansara Utama (Uptown), Petaling Jaya, Selangor (Greater KL), Malaysia
F.w: The nasi lemak many call Malaysia's best; queues since the 1980s for the ayam goreng berempah. Regulars have included prime ministers and national athletes.

F.ad: 18 Jalan Hang Jebat (Jonker Street), Malacca, Malaysia
F.w: The long-queued Jonker Street original of Malacca's signature rice-ball chicken rice, at the entrance to Jonker Walk; documented by Mark Wiens and in the MICHELIN Guide's chicken-rice feature.

F.ad: 327 Maha Chai Road, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok, Thailand
F.w: Bangkok's one-MICHELIN-star street stall; octogenarian chef Supinya 'Jay Fai' Junsuta cooks in ski goggles over charcoal. Held its star since 2018; now open Wed–Sat.

F.ad: 313-315 Maha Chai Road, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok, Thailand
F.w: The 'Pad Thai Pratu Phi' institution near the Grand Palace, cooking over charcoal since 1966; MICHELIN Guide-recommended and a fixture of every Bangkok food tour.

F.ad: 431-433 Tanao Road, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok, Thailand
F.w: An 80+-year family sticky-rice shop near the Grand Palace; MICHELIN Bib Gourmand for its mango sticky rice.

F.n: Nai Ek Roll Noodle (Nai Ek Kuay Jub)
F.ad: Soi Yaowarat 9, Yaowarat (Chinatown), Bangkok, Thailand
F.w: A Chinatown Bib Gourmand mainstay for aggressively peppery rolled-noodle soup and crispy pork.

F.ad: 29/1 Ratchaphuek Alley, Chang Phueak, Chiang Mai, Thailand
F.w: One of Chiang Mai's most famous khao soi houses; MICHELIN Guide-listed, with chicken and beef versions.

F.ad: Near Wat Kuan Kama, Sithiwongse Road, Old City, Chiang Mai, Thailand
F.w: The tiny lunch-only stall locals most often name as Chiang Mai's best khao soi; also a Mark Wiens pick.

F.ad: 49 Bat Dan Street, Hoan Kiem District, Hanoi, Vietnam
F.w: Hanoi's most famous old-school beef pho — order at the counter and queue; MICHELIN Bib Gourmand.

F.ad: 24 Le Van Huu Street, Hai Ba Trung District, Hanoi, Vietnam
F.w: The 'Obama bun cha' where Barack Obama and Anthony Bourdain dined in 2016 (Parts Unknown); now in the MICHELIN Guide Vietnam.

F.ad: 26 Le Thi Rieng Street, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: Saigon's most famous banh mi since 1989 — permanent queues for the thap cam loaded with pate and cold cuts.

F.ad: 84 Dang Van Ngu Street, Phu Nhuan District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
F.w: A Bib Gourmand com tam house famous for its thick, well-charred grilled pork chop over broken rice.

F.ad: 2B Phan Chau Trinh, Hoi An Ancient Town, Quang Nam, Vietnam
F.w: Made world-famous when Anthony Bourdain filmed here and called it a 'symphony in a sandwich'; the definitive Hoi An banh mi.

F.ad: Jl. Tegal Sari No. 2 (off Jl. Suweta, near Ubud Palace), Ubud, Bali, Indonesia
F.w: Ubud's most famous babi guling, from a recipe once cooked for the royal family; made globally famous by Anthony Bourdain. Lunch only, until the pork runs out.

F.ad: Jl. Kebon Sirih Raya (original branch), Central Jakarta, Indonesia
F.w: The original outlet of Jakarta's best-known satay house; a reliable, Lonely Planet-recommended introduction to Indonesian classics.

F.ad: Jl. Wijilan (near the Kraton), Yogyakarta, Indonesia
F.w: Yogyakarta's most famous 'dry' gudeg, run since ~1950; the benchmark for the city's signature dish.

F.ad: Jl. Blora, Central Jakarta, Indonesia
F.w: A respected Padang restaurant since 1973; its rendang landed it on Asia's 50 Best 'Essence of Asia'.

F.ad: One Mango Avenue (and branches), Cebu City, Philippines
F.w: The Cebu lechon Anthony Bourdain declared 'the best pig, ever' on his Philippines episode; founded by food writer Joel 'Marketman' Binamira.

F.ad: F. Cabahug Street, Mabolo (and branches), Cebu City, Philippines
F.w: Cebu's most internationally recognised lechon brand and pioneer of the spicy style, open since 1997.

F.ad: 432 San Andres Street cor Roxas Boulevard, Malate, Manila, Philippines
F.w: A Manila institution since 1936, 'home of the best chicken barbecue in town'; its Roxas Blvd home is a National Historical Commission-marked historic site.

F.ad: Ayala Triangle Gardens, Makati (flagship; branches across Metro Manila), Philippines
F.w: The Moment Group's beloved Filipino comfort-food chain; its flagship carries a MICHELIN Bib Gourmand and its crispy sisig is a signature.

F.ad: 77-79 Pansodan Street (Lower Block), Yangon, Myanmar
F.w: A restored colonial-era tea house downtown, widely loved for a polished mohinga and tea-leaf salad.

F.ad: Sala Kamreuk (Wat Damnak area), Siem Reap, Cambodia
F.w: Cambodia's most-awarded kitchen — a seasonal Khmer degustation applying French-trained rigour to local produce (ranked in OAD's Leading Restaurants of Asia).

F.ad: 74 Street 174, Phnom Penh, Cambodia
F.w: Country-style Khmer cooking (famous fish amok) in a French-colonial villa; a Friends International social enterprise training at-risk youth.

F.ad: Kingkitsarath Road (Nam Khan riverside), Luang Prabang, Laos
F.w: Luang Prabang's best-known 'Lao cuisine' restaurant and cooking school; a guided introduction to laap, jeow and the Lao sampling platter.

F.ad: #01-10/11 Maxwell Food Centre, 1 Kadayanallur Street
F.w: Singapore's most famous chicken rice stall; Michelin Bib Gourmand, feted by Bourdain & Ramsay.

F.ad: #01-07 Maxwell Food Centre, 1 Kadayanallur Street
F.w: The rival stall a few doors from Tian Tian; ex-Tian Tian chef, legendary dark soy & chilli.

F.n: Hawker Chan (Liao Fan Hong Kong Soya Sauce Chicken Rice & Noodle)
F.ad: 78 Smith Street, Chinatown
F.w: The world's first Michelin-starred hawker (2016); Smith St stall holds a Michelin Bib.

F.ad: #01-08 United Square, 101 Thomson Road, Novena
F.w: Founded 1987; a consistent big-name chicken rice institution ranked by Eatbook & Seth Lui.

F.ad: #02-66 Hong Lim Food Centre, 531A Upper Cross Street
F.w: Michelin Bib Gourmand three-peat; heritage cut-noodle laksa eaten spoon-only.

F.ad: 11 New Bridge Road, #01-01
F.w: Peppery Teochew bak kut teh; among only 17 stalls to hold a Michelin Bib across all 10 SG editions.

F.n: Hill Street Tai Hwa Pork Noodle
F.ad: #01-12 Block 466 Crawford Lane
F.w: One Michelin star since 2016; widely called Singapore's best bak chor mee, 1-2hr queues.

F.ad: #02-16 Hong Lim Food Centre, 531A Upper Cross Street
F.w: The other half of the Tai Hwa/Tai Wah lineage; Michelin Bib bak chor mee at Hong Lim.

F.ad: #02-48/49 Hong Lim Food Centre, 531A Upper Cross Street
F.w: Upgraded from Selected to Michelin Bib Gourmand in the 2025 guide; old-school wanton mee.

F.ad: 30 Foch Road, Lavender
F.w: Cult wanton mee known for its near-soupy, lard-based chilli gravy.

F.ad: #01-15 Pek Kio Market & Food Centre, 41A Cambridge Road
F.w: Michelin-listed since 1951; intense all-prawn broth, the 'auntie with attitude'.

F.n: Best Satay 7 & 8 (Lau Pa Sat Satay Street)
F.ad: Boon Tat Street / Lau Pa Sat, 18 Raffles Quay
F.w: The most popular stalls on Lau Pa Sat's evening Satay Street, grilled over charcoal.

F.ad: 11 & 15 Jalan Pisang, Kampong Glam
F.w: The benchmark nasi padang near Kampong Glam; long-time Michelin Bib Gourmand.

F.ad: 138 Race Course Road, Little India
F.w: Pioneered South-Indian fish head curry (1969); Michelin Bib Gourmand, the local go-to.

F.ad: #01-232 Tekka Centre, 665 Buffalo Road, Little India
F.w: Tekka's most popular biryani stall since 1968; Michelin-recognised.

F.ad: 76-78 Serangoon Road, Little India
F.w: Heritage vegetarian South Indian since 1947; the gold standard for masala thosai.

F.ad: 697-699 North Bridge Road, Kampong Glam
F.w: Founded 1908 opposite Sultan Mosque; the most famous Indian-Muslim murtabak specialist.

F.ad: #02-008 Chinatown Complex Food Centre, 335 Smith Street
F.w: Artisanal chendol with cold-pressed coconut milk & charcoal-brewed gula melaka, from $2.

F.n: Ya Kun Kaya Toast (Far East Square)
F.ad: #01-01 Far East Square, 18 China Street
F.w: Founded 1944; the flagship still grills wafer-thin charcoal kaya toast, SG's kopitiam icon.

F.ad: 35 Keong Saik Road, Chinatown
F.w: In Keong Saik since 1939; one of the very few still doing old-school thrice-toasted kaya toast.

F.n: Beach Road Scissors Cut Curry Rice
F.ad: 229 Jalan Besar (Corner of Jalan Besar & Kitchener Road)
F.w: Since 1930; the definitive scissor-cut Hainanese curry rice, ingredients snipped to order.

F.ad: #02-67/68 Tiong Bahru Market, 30 Seng Poh Road
F.w: Since 1946; three-day curry, one dish only, perpetual Tiong Bahru queue.

F.n: Jian Bo Tiong Bahru Shui Kueh
F.ad: #02-05 Tiong Bahru Market, 30 Seng Poh Road
F.w: Since 1958; the most renowned chwee kueh stall, Michelin-listed.

F.ad: 183-191 Jalan Besar
F.w: Since 1962; Singapore's beloved late-night dim sum institution (open till the small hours).

F.ad: #01-73 Newton Food Centre, 500 Clemenceau Avenue North
F.w: Juicy-oyster orh luak with crispy edges; new Michelin Bib Gourmand.

F.ad: #01-32 CT Hub, 2 Kallang Avenue
F.w: Opened 2024, straight onto the 2025 Michelin Bib list; Malaysian-style ayam goreng berempah.

F.ad: #01-91 Newton Food Centre, 500 Clemenceau Avenue North
F.w: Comforting Teochew fish porridge with deboned mackerel; new to the 2025 Michelin Bib list.

F.ad: #02-06 Tiong Bahru Market, 30 Seng Poh Road
F.w: Michelin-approved handmade Teochew fishballs & fishcake.

F.ad: #01-27 Newton Food Centre, 500 Clemenceau Avenue North
F.w: Newton's iconic sambal stingray & satay hub, featured in Crazy Rich Asians.

F.ad: #01-01/02 Riverside Point, 30 Merchant Road, Clarke Quay
F.w: Singapore's most famous chilli crab name (since 1987); sweet-spicy gravy mopped up with mantou.

F.ad: #01-04 National Gallery Singapore, 1 St Andrew's Road
F.w: Three Michelin stars; Chef Julien Royer's flagship, a perennial Asia's 50 Best fixture.

F.ad: 51 East Coast Road, Katong
F.w: The definitive Katong laksa that 'beat' Gordon Ramsay; former Michelin Bib, cut noodles eaten with a spoon.

F.ad: #01-32 Old Airport Road Food Centre, 51 Old Airport Road
F.w: Serving one dish since 1960; drier prawn-stock Hokkien mee with a Michelin Bib Gourmand.

F.ad: #01-41 Bedok South Market & Food Centre, 16 Bedok South Road
F.w: Since 1961; full-bodied wok-hei char kway teow with cockles, a Michelin Bib and 40-min queues.

F.n: Lao Fu Zi Fried Kway Teow
F.ad: #01-12 Old Airport Road Food Centre, 51 Old Airport Road
F.w: Smoky wok-hei CKT with blood cockles & lup cheong; a 2025 Michelin Bib Gourmand.

F.ad: #01-135/136 Old Airport Road Food Centre, 51 Old Airport Road
F.w: Teochew kway chap since the 1980s; immaculately cleaned braised offal, a 2025 Michelin Bib.

F.ad: #01-121 Old Airport Road Food Centre, 51 Old Airport Road
F.w: KL-style caramelised char siew on pork belly; a modern hawker favourite.

F.ad: 204 East Coast Road, Katong/Joo Chiat
F.w: 101-year-old Hainanese kopitiam; iconic round charcoal kaya buns, reopened 2021.

F.ad: 38/40 Joo Chiat Place, Joo Chiat
F.w: Singapore's oldest Peranakan restaurant (1953); traditional Nonya cooking, third generation.

F.n: Mr & Mrs Mohgan's Super Crispy Roti Prata
F.ad: 300 Joo Chiat Road (Tin Yeang Coffeeshop)
F.w: Cult super-crispy prata cooked to order; long morning queues, 'cult status entirely affirmed'.

F.ad: 237 Geylang Road (Geylang Lorong 9)
F.w: Iconic Geylang beef hor fun with goopy black bean gravy; in the 2025 Michelin Guide.

F.ad: #01-05 East Coast Lagoon Food Village, 1220 East Coast Parkway
F.w: East Coast Lagoon's beloved Malay-Muslim satay, grilled seaside over charcoal.

F.n: Kway Guan Huat Joo Chiat Popiah
F.ad: 95 Joo Chiat Road, Joo Chiat
F.w: Since 1938; hand-made popiah skins spun on a wooden pole, a Joo Chiat heritage name.

F.n: Sin Heng Claypot Bak Koot Teh
F.ad: #01-01, 439 Joo Chiat Road, Joo Chiat
F.w: 40-year-old claypot bak kut teh with pepper & garlic; a 2025 Michelin Bib Gourmand.

F.ad: 247 Joo Chiat Place, Joo Chiat (original; premises sold Aug 2025)
F.w: The legendary Joo Chiat/Still Road black pepper crab; original shophouse closed Aug 2025 after the premises sold (crew relocated to a Tampines industrial canteen).

F.ad: #01-15 Adam Road Food Centre, 2 Adam Road, Bukit Timah
F.w: Michelin Bib Gourmand nasi lemak on basmati; reportedly a favourite of the Sultan of Brunei.

F.ad: 1 Thong Soon Avenue, Upper Thomson
F.w: Famous Upper Thomson prata with 60+ flavours from the Murtaburger to Prata Alfredo.

F.ad: Block 17A Dempsey Road, Dempsey Hill
F.w: The world's first Michelin-starred Peranakan restaurant; Chef Malcolm Lee's elevated Straits-Chinese cooking.

F.ad: 7 Dempsey Road, Dempsey Hill
F.w: One Michelin star & Asia's 50 Best; wood-fired modern barbecue, near-impossible reservations.

F.ad: 399/401/403 Balestier Road
F.w: A chicken rice institution since 1979; promoted to Michelin Bib Gourmand in 2025.

F.ad: 347 Balestier Road
F.w: Peppery Teochew bak kut teh open late for supper; a Balestier landmark.

F.n: Margaret Drive Sin Kee Chicken Rice
F.ad: #02-06 Holland Drive Market & Food Centre, 44 Holland Drive
F.w: Steamed chicken rice since 1978; on the Michelin Bib Gourmand list since 2018.

F.n: Depot Road Zhen Shan Mei Claypot Laksa
F.ad: #01-75 Alexandra Village Food Centre, 120 Bukit Merah Lane 1
F.w: Multi-time award-winning laksa (Michelin Bib 2016+) rich with cockles and prawns.

F.ad: #02-185 Bukit Timah Market & Food Centre, 51 Upper Bukit Timah Road
F.w: Famous white chai tow kway near Beauty World; crisp, wok-fried and eggy.

F.ad: #01-49 Redhill Food Centre, 85 Redhill Lane
F.w: 'Mickey Mouse' chai tow kway, radish cake made from scratch daily; Michelin Bib since 2019.

F.ad: #01-06 Commonwealth Crescent Market & Food Centre, 31 Commonwealth Crescent
F.w: Charcoal-roasted char siew with an ideal fat-to-meat ratio; reopened after a two-year hiatus.

F.ad: #01-120 ABC Brickworks Market & Food Centre, 6 Jalan Bukit Merah
F.w: 34 years of sweet, succulent char siew and roast meats at ABC Brickworks.

F.ad: #01-40 Yuhua Village Market & Food Centre, 254 Jurong East Street 24
F.w: Charcoal-roasted meats & wanton mee in Jurong East; Michelin Bib Gourmand.

F.ad: Block 505 Jurong West Street 52 (Jurong West 505 Market & Food Centre)
F.w: Nostalgic old-school wanton mee in Jurong West; new to the 2025 Michelin Guide.

F.ad: #01-06 Boon Lay Place Food Village, 221B Boon Lay Place
F.w: A big-name Jurong nasi lemak using extra-virgin coconut oil.

F.ad: Toa Payoh West Market & Food Centre, #02-30, Blk 127 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, S310127
F.w: Michelin Bib Gourmand since 2016 — two sisters fry each plate of crispy-yet-spongy white carrot cake to order, drawing long queues at the freshly renovated (reopened Aug 2025) Toa Payoh West hawker centre.

F.n: Come Daily Fried Hokkien Prawn Mee
F.ad: Toa Payoh West Market & Food Centre, #02-27, Blk 127 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, S310127
F.w: Michelin-listed and running since 1968, Steven Ng reduces prawn stock right in the wok for one of Toa Payoh's most famous plates of Hokkien mee — a fixture of the reopened Toa Payoh West food centre.

F.n: Hai Nan Xing Zhou Beef Noodle
F.ad: Kim Keat Palm Market & Food Centre, #01-06, Blk 22 Lorong 7 Toa Payoh, S310022
F.w: Nearly 70 years of Hainanese beef noodles from S$5, newly awarded a Michelin Bib Gourmand — dry or soup, in a rich braise the whole hawker centre queues for.

F.ad: Block A, Jackson Square, 11 Toa Payoh Lorong 3, S319579
F.w: A Michelin-starred Cantonese chef sells $5 wanton mee from a warehouse-canteen stall — HK-shipped springy noodles and charred char siew that earned a Michelin Bib Gourmand within a year of opening (still listed 2025/2026).

F.ad: Kim Keat Palm Market & Food Centre, #01-20, Blk 22 Lorong 7 Toa Payoh, S310022
F.w: The original stall of Singapore's 58-year-old fishball dynasty (est. 1968), Michelin Bib Gourmand for four years running since 2022 — springy, umami yellowtail fishballs made fresh daily.

F.ad: Blk 20 Toa Payoh Lorong 7 coffeeshop, S310020
F.w: A beloved $1 nasi lemak that has held its price since 1987 to stay affordable for elderly regulars — cooking starts at 4am and 300-500 plates sell out by midday; covered by every major food outlet and YouTuber Ghib Ojisan.

F.ad: Toa Payoh Lorong 5 Food Centre, #01-31, Blk 75 Lorong 5 Toa Payoh, S310075
F.w: A cult chicken rice stall that swaps roast/poached chicken for addictively marinated crispy fried wings ($3.50) with a spicy chilli dip — famously long evening queues until sold out.

F.ad: Blk 22 Lorong 7 Toa Payoh, #01-58, S310022
F.w: The Toa Payoh outlet of Uncle David Ng's famed noodle stall, where bouncy yellowtail fishballs are hand-pounded on the spot (the Holland Drive original holds the Michelin Bib Gourmand).

F.ad: Kim Keat Palm Market & Food Centre, #01-03, Blk 22 Lorong 7 Toa Payoh, S310022
F.w: A 3rd-generation popiah stall with roots to 1930, hand-rolling Hokkien-style popiah (no pork, no lard, no MSG) with house-fried sole-fish crisps — one of Singapore's most heritage popiah names.

F.n: Lai Heng Mushroom Minced Meat Noodle
F.ad: Blk 73 Toa Payoh Lorong 5, Toa Payoh
F.w: A bak chor mee institution running since 1985 (relocated twice within Toa Payoh), still turning out a spicy dry mee kia and a standout lard-rich kway teow soup that Seth Lui rated after 24 years of visits.

F.ad: Toa Payoh West Market & Food Centre, #02-34, Blk 127 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, S310127
F.w: UK-trained ex-engineer Anton Tan turned his family's zi char stall into a viral $1.20 muffin institution — deliberately misshapen buns with crunchy caramelised crusts; a long-queue hawker-dessert cult reopened after the 2025 renovation.

F.ad: Toa Payoh West Market & Food Centre, Blk 127 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, S310127
F.w: A 30-plus-year heritage pau stall (est. 1993, three years on the Michelin Plate) hand-making Teochew-style buns with thick, not-too-sweet lotus paste — announced closure end-2025 but reopened June 2026 after public demand.

F.ad: Toa Payoh West Market & Food Centre, Blk 127 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, S310127
F.w: Two sisters plate one of Singapore's most generous $5 thunder tea rice sets — less oil, less salt, no MSG — with the fragrant bitter-green tea broth poured over brown rice and crunchy toppings.

F.ad: Toa Payoh West Market & Food Centre, Blk 127 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, S310127
F.w: Ex-Italian-restaurant cook Desheng makes beancurd from scratch daily with non-GMO soybeans — smooth, un-gritty tau huay you can dress with gula melaka, grass jelly or gingko.

F.n: Toa Payoh Scissors Cut Curry Rice
F.ad: Toa Payoh Lorong 8 Market & Food Centre, 210 Lorong 8 Toa Payoh, S310210
F.w: Old-school Hainanese-style curry rice from S$2.80 — a heaped plate of chopped sides flooded in three different gravies (curry, braise, pork), a comfort-food fixture of Lorong 8.

F.n: Uncle Kun's Delicacies (Kun Shu Food Stall)
F.ad: Toa Payoh Vista Market, Lorong 4 Toa Payoh
F.w: Ex-hotel HK chef Lam Kun serves restaurant-grade dim sum at hawker prices; his signature oblong scallop glutinous rice (S$4.80), packed with dried scallop, salted egg and lap cheong, isn't found elsewhere in Singapore.

F.n: Min Kee Tanjong Rhu Wanton Noodle
F.ad: Kim Keat Palm Market & Food Centre, Blk 22 Lorong 7 Toa Payoh, S310022
F.w: A decades-old wanton mee that relocated from Tanjong Rhu, still selling a substantial $3.50 bowl of springy noodles with black-chilli option, soupy and fried wantons — a Kim Keat breakfast favourite.

F.ad: Gourmet Paradise Food Court, Toa Payoh HDB Hub, Blk 480 Lorong 6 Toa Payoh, #B1-01, S310480
F.w: Likely the last hawker hand-making this Teochew snack from scratch — Teo Yong Joo mills flour, roasts peanuts and pinches each soft, tender muah chee ball to order at the HDB Hub food court.

F.ad: Blk 92 Toa Payoh Lorong 4, #01-264, S310092
F.w: Once rated among Singapore's top-five Hokkien mee — served in a heat-retaining claypot with deep-fried crispy pork belly — this 10-year Toa Payoh favourite shuttered on 28 Feb 2026. Kept here as a flagged closure.

F.n: Hup Chong Hakka Yong Tau Foo — CLOSED
F.ad: Blk 203 Toa Payoh (final location; earlier Blk 116/124)
F.w: A four-generation Hakka yong tau foo with roots to a 1952 pushcart, famous for handmade fried meatballs and fish paste — it closed for good on 28 Jan 2026 after 70-plus years amid falling footfall. Kept here as a flagged closure.

F.ad: Toa Payoh West Market & Food Centre, #02-22, Blk 127 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, S310127
F.w: A father-and-son team from Shenzhen mill their own rice flour on a stone grinder to make thicker, rustic cheung fun to order, tinted naturally with spinach and pink dragonfruit across 13 fillings — a standout of the reopened (Aug 2025) Toa Payoh West hawker centre.

F.ad: Toa Payoh West Market & Food Centre, #02-24, Blk 127 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, S310127
F.w: A no-frills stall doing a $3 bowl of fried fish ban mian — crispy fried fish slices, handmade noodles and a clean savoury broth — one of the value picks flagged across guides to the renovated Toa Payoh West food centre.

F.ad: Toa Payoh West Market & Food Centre, Blk 127 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, S310127
F.w: A 20-year veteran hand-tearing mee hoon kueh dough to order and ladling fish soup and porridge — old-school comfort noodles that regulars queue for at Toa Payoh West.

F.ad: Toa Payoh Lorong 8 Market & Food Centre, #01-79, Blk 210 Lorong 8 Toa Payoh, S310210
F.w: The Toa Payoh outlet of the Tekka Centre briyani institution — a Michelin Plate / Michelin-recommended name whose fragrant $6 chicken, mutton and fish briyani draw a queue; the pull-apart rice and house sambal are the draw.

F.ad: Toa Payoh Lorong 8 Market & Food Centre, #01-24, Blk 210 Lorong 8 Toa Payoh, S310210
F.w: A 40-year Toa Payoh institution famous for selling out fast — owner Mr Ng meticulously cleans the offal for an odourless, tender braise served over silky rice sheets in a light herbal broth; widely rated among Singapore's best kway chap.

F.ad: 211 Lorong 8 Toa Payoh, #01-01, S310211
F.w: An ex-hotel chef plates restaurant-grade Japanese food from a kopitiam beside the Lorong 8 hawker centre — the Tataki Salmon Roll ($6) and Butter Yaki Seabass Bento ($6.80) look far pricier than they cost; nothing on the menu tops $10.

F.n: Da Lao Fried White Kway Teow
F.ad: Toa Payoh Lorong 8 Market & Food Centre, #01-23, Blk 210 Lorong 8 Toa Payoh, S310210
F.w: A one-man wok turning out Penang-style fried white kway teow with serious wok hei — clean, coated-not-greasy strands with fish cake, lap cheong and cockles from $4; the single-hand pace means a wait, and a long queue.

F.n: Seletar Sheng Mian Mee Hoon Kway
F.ad: Toa Payoh Lorong 8 Market & Food Centre, Blk 210 Lorong 8 Toa Payoh, S310210
F.w: Relocated from the demolished Seletar market, this snaking-queue stall hand-kneads, smacks and tears each piece of dough for uniquely textured sheng mian in a comforting pork-and-ikan-bilis broth from $3.

F.ad: Toa Payoh Lorong 8 Market & Food Centre, #01-07, Blk 210 Lorong 8 Toa Payoh, S310210
F.w: Widely dubbed the best cendol in Singapore — and a favourite of ESM Goh Chok Tong, whose photos line the stall — with firmly-packed ice that stays solid, springy pandan jelly and gula melaka, plus Mao Shan Wang / D24 durian tops.

F.n: Song Kee Kway Teow Noodle Soup
F.ad: Toa Payoh Lorong 5 Food Centre, Blk 75 Lorong 5 Toa Payoh, S310075
F.w: A 16-year evening-only stall (5pm–midnight) whose fishballs are pounded from scratch at 3am — bouncy, fresh yellowtail fishballs and fragrant fish dumplings over springy mee pok that fans call the best in Singapore.

F.ad: Toa Payoh Lorong 5 Food Centre, #01-25, Blk 75 Lorong 5 Toa Payoh, S310075
F.w: A 1966 satay stall now in its third generation, grilling well-marinated Chinese-style chicken and pork skewers over charcoal to order — beautifully charred sticks served with peanut sauce and fresh pineapple gravy.

F.ad: Kim Keat Palm Market & Food Centre, #01-25, Blk 22 Lorong 7 Toa Payoh, S310022
F.w: A 50-year-old orh chien specialist (open ~3 hours a day) frying crisp-yet-chewy potato-starch batter with fluffy egg and juicy large Korean oysters, finished with crunchy parsley — a repeat pick on 'best oyster omelette' lists.

F.ad: Kim Keat Palm Market & Food Centre, Blk 22 Lorong 7 Toa Payoh, S310022
F.w: The stall with Kim Keat Palm's longest breakfast queue — wok-fried bee hoon and noodles with cabbage, best paired with a runny-yolk sunny-side-up egg; a heartland morning staple.

F.ad: Toa Payoh Palm Spring Market, Blk 93 Lorong 4 Toa Payoh, S310093
F.w: A second-generation kway chap running since 1967 and rated Singapore's best-rated kway chap — spice-forward braised innards, tau pok and silky rice sheets from 5.30pm, with snaking queues before it even opens.

F.ad: Toa Payoh Palm Spring Market, Blk 93 Lorong 4 Toa Payoh, S310093
F.w: A 58-year cult favourite with arguably the longest queue in Palm Spring from 6am — springy mee pok tossed in a punchy chilli sauce with hand-made fishballs and meatballs; dry or soup.

F.ad: Toa Payoh Vista Market, 74 Lorong 4 Toa Payoh, S310074
F.w: A Vista Market morning fixture drawing daily queues for crisp roti prata — plain to cheese-and-egg and sweet banana — then Indian-Muslim mee goreng, nasi goreng merah and tulang merah after 1.30pm; carries a Makansutra 'Divine' rating.

F.ad: Gourmet Paradise Food Court, Toa Payoh HDB Hub, #B1-01, Blk 480 Lorong 6 Toa Payoh, S310480
F.w: A decades-old rojak stall by the HDB Hub food-court escalator with a permanent 20-30 minute queue — a generous mountain of youtiao, cucumber, pineapple, turnip and cuttlefish drowned in prawn-paste, torch-ginger and mounds of peanut.

F.n: Biang Biang Noodles Xi'an Famous Food
F.ad: Food Alley, 190 Lorong 6 Toa Payoh, #01-518, Toa Payoh Central, S310190
F.w: A rare hawker source of Xi'an biang biang noodles — extra-wide belt noodles hand-stretched and slapped against the counter, tossed with braised pork, tomato-egg and chilli, plus rou jia mo (Chinese 'burger'); a hidden gem at Toa Payoh Central's Food Alley.

F.ad: Blk 73 Lorong 4 Toa Payoh, #01-585, S310073
F.w: A young-hawker zi char revival — five friends in their late twenties reopened a founder's father's stall, cooking almost a hundred dishes rich in wok hei at hawker prices, from sambal kang kong to inventive Imperial Cereal Milk Pork.

F.ad: Blk 125 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, #01-, S310125
F.w: A husband-and-wife stall (she's Vietnamese) doing soul-comforting pho with broth simmered 8 hours on beef shank and shin, plus crisp fried spring rolls stuffed with pork, prawn and glass noodles — sauces imported from Vietnam, everything under $10.

F.ad: Blk 128 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, #01-829, S310128
F.w: The original heartland home of a beloved SG ice-cream name — handcrafted scoops like Earl Grey Lavender and Sea Salt Gula Melaka over freshly-pressed, crisp-outside pillowy Belgian waffles; the Toa Payoh dessert stop.

F.ad: Blk 128 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, #01-833, S310128
F.w: An under-rated heartland cafe run by a France-trained baker — everything is handmade in-house, from crusty tiger bread and light not-too-sweet cakes to a Nyonya chendol waffle; a quaint wooden-front hideout beside Creamier.

F.ad: Blk 85C Lorong 4 Toa Payoh, #01-385, S310085
F.w: A hole-in-the-wall HDB cake cafe by three pastry-chef friends selling atas bakes from $3.50 — the chio Watermelon Rose cake (a nod to Black Star Pastry) and fudgy brownies among biscotti, pound cakes and cookies.
